To check a render before you commit it, render the chart as Argo CD does. --skip-tests leaves out the test Pod, as Argo CD does:

helm template hangar oci://ghcr.io/hangar-hub/charts/hangar --namespace hangar -f values.yaml --skip-tests

To rotate a credential in the Secret, create a Secret with a new name and change existingSecret: the Pods' checksum/secret annotation covers the name, so the Pods restart and read it. Under helm upgrade, the chart also reads the Secret's data, so changing it in place restarts the Pods on the next upgrade.

With persistence on (SQLite in one Pod), you can instead set generateSecrets: false and leave the Instance key and admin password unset: Hangar generates them on its volume on first start and prints the password once in its log.

docs.title: Values
docs.text:
Value What it does publicURL Required. server.public_url. config Any configuration, rendered into a ConfigMap as hangar.yaml. secrets, existingSecret HANGAR_* variables in a Secret the chart writes, or one you manage. generateSecrets Generate the Instance key and admin password when you do not set them (default on). Needs helm install or helm upgrade; renders without cluster access stop with an error. migrations.mode hook (default): a pre-install and pre-upgrade Job. initContainer: an init container in each web and worker Pod, for GitOps tools. migrations.waitForDatabase With migrations.mode: initContainer, how long the init container waits for the database to answer before it fails. Default 5m. persistence.* SQLite and filesystem mode on a PersistentVolumeClaim (default on). web.*, worker.* Replicas, resources, autoscaling (HPA on CPU, which needs the metrics server in the cluster), PodDisruptionBudget, node selection and topology spread. ingress.* An Ingress; datasetsServerHost: true also routes datasets-server.<host>, which the datasets library calls. httpRoute.* A Gateway API HTTPRoute instead of the Ingress. serviceAccount.annotations For IRSA or Workload Identity. metrics.* A Prometheus port and an optional ServiceMonitor. networkPolicy.* An optional NetworkPolicy. cacheSizeLimit, tmpSizeLimit Sizes of the emptyDir volumes for the git pack cache (default 16Gi) and /tmp. The pack cache goes over git.cache_size (10GiB by default) while Repos are in use, so the chart requires cacheSizeLimit to be at least a quarter larger; the kubelet evicts a Pod whose emptyDir passes its limit. drainDelaySeconds Seconds a terminating Pod keeps serving before Hangar closes its listener, so requests routed to it during a rolling update still succeed (default 5). A preStop sleep on Kubernetes 1.30 and later, server.drain_delay on 1.29. 0 turns it off. extraEnv, extraEnvFrom, extraVolumes, extraVolumeMounts Anything else.

Every Pod runs as non-root with a read-only root filesystem, no privilege escalation, every capability dropped and the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile. helm test checks /readyz from inside the cluster.

The full list is in the chart's values.yaml.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: To load models into other Pods in the cluster from Hangar, without downloading them on every Pod start, see Load models in Kubernetes.

docs.title: Point HF_ENDPOINT at Hangar
docs.text:
Hugging Face libraries read the Hub's address from HF_ENDPOINT, and a Token from HF_TOKEN. Set both and they use Hangar:

export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hangar.example.com
export HF_TOKEN=hgr_...
export DISABLE_SAFETENSORS_CONVERSION=1

hangar env prints these for the Instance you signed in to:

eval "$(hangar env)"

DISABLE_SAFETENSORS_CONVERSION=1 matters for models that only have pickle weights (pytorch_model.bin). Without it, transformers may send the Repo ID, and a Token you passed to it, to a conversion service on huggingface.co. Hangar also refuses the request transformers makes before that call, so the leak cannot happen, but setting the variable avoids the attempt.

Now every Hub call goes to Hangar. The Repo must be in the Arsenal, so pull it first, as in Pull your first model; a Repo that is not there answers as if it did not exist, unless an admin turned on Pull-through:

from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-bert")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-bert")

Files land in the usual cache, ~/.cache/huggingface/hub, which the hangar CLI shares.

docs.title: In Python only
docs.text:
import os
os.environ["HF_ENDPOINT"] = "https://hangar.example.com"   # before importing huggingface_hub

or pass endpoint= to HfApi, hf_hub_download and snapshot_download.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
datasets also calls datasets-server.<host>. Point that name at Hangar too, which serves the Dataset Viewer API there; see Datasets.

More: Python libraries.

docs.title: System requirements and sizing
docs.text: Hangar is one binary that runs as a container or on a host. Most of what it needs is disk space for the models and datasets you keep.

docs.title: Software
docs.text:
Install Needs Container image Docker or Kubernetes, on linux/amd64 or linux/arm64. The image includes git. Binary git 2.39 or later on the PATH for the server. The client commands do not need git. Helm chart Kubernetes 1.29 or later. Scaled out Postgres (CI tests 18) and an S3-compatible bucket or a shared filesystem.

Tested versions and platforms lists what CI runs on.

docs.title: CPU and memory
docs.text: The Helm chart's defaults are a reasonable start for one web or worker process: a request of 250m CPU and 256 MiB of memory, and a memory limit of 1 GiB. In the benchmarks, a web replica limited to 2 CPUs and 1 GiB peaked at 66 to 115 MiB of memory while it served four concurrent 1 GiB uploads or 140 GiB of downloads. The benchmarks did not measure worker processes, which run Pulls, indexing and Parquet exports; watch their memory with the metrics Hangar exports, and raise the limit if your datasets need it.

docs.title: Disk
docs.text:
What Default location How much The Blob store storage.fs.path (/var/lib/hangar/blobs), or a bucket About the total size of the files you pull and upload. Each LFS object is stored once per Instance, however many Repos hold it, and a Partial mirror holds only the files you pulled. The database database.dsn (/var/lib/hangar/hangar.db), or Postgres Metadata only: Repos, refs, Jobs, users and the audit log, not file contents. The git pack cache git.cache_dir (/var/cache/hangar/git) git.cache_size, 10 GiB by default, plus about a quarter more, because the cache goes over its limit while Repos are in use. It is disposable. Temporary files TMPDIR (/tmp in the image) On S3, one part per upload in progress: 16 MiB for objects up to 156 GiB, more for larger ones. The Helm chart gives /tmp 2 GiB.

Space is not freed at once when content goes away. A deleted Repo can be restored for repos.restore_window (7 days), and garbage collection deletes LFS objects that no Repo references once they are older than gc.grace_period (7 days). See Storage backends.

docs.title: The pack cache in memory
docs.text:
The read-only docker run example and deploy/compose/quickstart.yaml mount /var/cache/hangar as a tmpfs. A tmpfs keeps its files in memory, so the pack cache then uses RAM, not disk. On a small host, give the tmpfs a size and keep the cache below it, or mount a volume there instead:

docker run -d --name hangar -p 8080:8080 -v hangar:/var/lib/hangar \
  --read-only --tmpfs /tmp --tmpfs /var/cache/hangar:uid=65532,gid=65532,size=4g \
  -e HANGAR_SERVER_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost:8080 \
  -e HANGAR_GIT_CACHE_SIZE=3GiB \
  ghcr.io/hangar-hub/hangar:latest

The Helm chart uses an emptyDir for the cache, sized with cacheSizeLimit (16 GiB by default), and refuses a limit less than a quarter larger than git.cache_size.

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
Direction What Into Hangar Clients reach server.public_url, port 8080 in the image. The datasets library also needs the datasets-server.<host> name; see Datasets. Into the store On S3 in redirect download mode or direct upload mode (the defaults), clients also reach the bucket's endpoint. Use proxy for both if they cannot. Out of Hangar Upstreams, such as huggingface.co, and the hosts their downloads redirect to; OIDC providers; webhook targets; and an OpenTelemetry endpoint if you set one. Nothing else.

An air-gapped Instance needs no internet access at all.

docs.title: Scaled out
docs.text: On the reference setup in Scaling, two web replicas with 2 vCPU and 1 GiB each, one worker, Postgres and MinIO meet Hangar's targets. Each process opens up to database.max_open_conns (20) connections to Postgres, so allow for that many per replica in Postgres's max_connections.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
Task-focused guides for using Hangar with the tools you already have.

  • Python and Hugging Face tools: Python libraries, the hf CLI, uploading, datasets, vLLM.
  • Other clients: git and git-lfs, Ollama, LM Studio, the hangar CLI.
  • Filling the Arsenal: importing an existing cache, pull windows and bandwidth, air-gapped Instances, gated models.
  • Teams, CI and clusters: a private Ollama registry, one model cache for a team, rate limits and slow downloads in CI, models in Kubernetes.
  • Organising and automating: Collections, webhooks.

docs.title: Air-gapped Instances
docs.text:
An Instance with no internet access can be fed from another Hangar Instance that has internet access.

  1. Run an outer Instance with internet access, and pull what the inner network needs into it.
  2. On the inner Instance, add the outer one as an Upstream: Admin, Upstreams, Add upstream, with its URL and a read Token for it as the Instance token. Or in configuration:
upstreams:
  outer:
    base_url: https://hangar-outer.example.com
    enabled: true
    token: hgr_...
  huggingface:
    enabled: false
  1. Pull from it like from huggingface.co: Discover lets you choose the Upstream, and the CLI takes --upstream outer:
hangar pull bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M --upstream outer

Mirrors keep the Repo IDs and Commit SHAs from the outer Instance, which kept them from huggingface.co, so HF_ENDPOINT swaps still work inside.

docs.title: Keep the web UI on the inside
docs.text:
The web UI links to the documentation at https://hangar.page/, for example from the explanation that opens when you hover over or click a badge such as Unsafe imports. On a network without internet access, point those links at a copy of the documentation, or turn them off, with ui.docs_url (HANGAR_UI_DOCS_URL).

To use a copy, build the documentation from the Hangar source at the release tag your Instance runs, on a machine with internet access, and serve the site folder on the inside. The copy must serve the same paths as https://hangar.page/, such as concepts/mirrors/. hangar version prints the version, and so does Admin, System in the web UI. For version 1.2.3:

git clone --branch v1.2.3 https://github.com/hangar-hub/hangar.git
cd hangar
uv run --no-project --with-requirements docs/requirements.txt mkdocs build

The build downloads the fonts, and the script that draws the native API reference, into site, so the copy loads nothing from the internet. Copies built from 1.2.3 and earlier releases load that script from cdn.jsdelivr.net, so their Native API page stays blank without internet access; the other pages work.

Then set the URL of the copy:

HANGAR_UI_DOCS_URL=https://docs.internal.example.com/hangar/

To remove the links, set HANGAR_UI_DOCS_URL= (empty), or docs_url: "" under ui in the configuration file. The explanations still show, without the link.

Also turn off Load external images in cards under Admin, Settings, so Model cards do not try to load images from the internet.

docs.title: Fully disconnected networks
docs.text: If no connection is allowed at all, move data with a backup instead: back up the outer Instance (hangar admin backup), carry the folder across, and restore it into the inner one (hangar admin restore). See Backup and restore. Or carry a Hugging Face cache across and run hangar import --from-hf-cache --offline on the inside.

docs.title: Avoid Hugging Face rate limits and slow downloads in CI
docs.text: CI jobs often start with an empty Hugging Face cache, so every run downloads the same models from huggingface.co again. With parallel jobs and a test matrix, that can add up to enough requests to reach huggingface.co's rate limits, and the downloads slow every run down.

docs.title: The errors
docs.text:
When a client reaches a rate limit, huggingface.co answers with HTTP status 429 Too Many Requests. Recent versions of huggingface_hub raise HfHubHTTPError with a message such as:

429 Too Many Requests: you have reached your 'resolvers' rate limit.
Retry after 120 seconds (0/3000 requests remaining in current 300s window).
Url: https://huggingface.co/...

From version 1.2.0, before it gives up, huggingface_hub waits until the limit resets and retries, and logs lines such as Rate limited. Waiting 121.0s before retry [Retry 1/5]., which makes a job slow rather than failed. Versions before 1.0, built on requests, show the error with this message:

429 Client Error: Too Many Requests for url: https://huggingface.co/...

transformers, datasets, sentence-transformers and vLLM download with huggingface_hub, so they show the same errors.

docs.title: Why CI reaches the limits
docs.text:
Hugging Face sets separate limits for API calls, for file downloads (which it calls resolvers) and for web pages, counted over 5-minute windows. Requests without a token count against the limit of the IP address they come from, which is the lowest limit. Requests with a token count against that account's limit. See Hub rate limits for the current numbers.

CI makes this worse:

  • Each job, and each cell of a test matrix, downloads the models again unless something restores a cache.
  • Loading a model makes several requests, one for each file and some for metadata, so a test suite that loads a few models makes many.
  • Workflows for pull requests from forks do not get your repository's secrets, so they run without HF_TOKEN even when other workflows have it.

docs.title: Fixes that need nothing new
docs.text:
These help whether or not you run Hangar:

  1. Set HF_TOKEN in every job that downloads, so requests count against your account rather than the runner's IP address. This is the first fix Hugging Face's rate limits page suggests.
  2. Keep the Hugging Face cache between runs. In GitHub Actions, restore ~/.cache/huggingface/hub with actions/cache, as in the example below.
  3. Load models at a Commit SHA (revision= in Python, --revision for hf download), so every run loads the same files, and change the cache key when you change a Revision.
  4. With the cache restored, set HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 for the test step, so the libraries load from the cache without making any requests.

A cache still misses when the key changes or when GitHub evicts it, and every miss downloads from huggingface.co again.

docs.title: Serve models to CI from Hangar
docs.text: A Hangar Instance keeps one copy of each model and serves it with the Hugging Face Hub API. With HF_ENDPOINT pointing at it, CI downloads from your Instance, and huggingface.co sees one download per file, from Hangar's Pull. Hangar does not rate-limit downloads.

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text:
1. Run an Instance that the runners can reach. GitHub-hosted runners connect from the internet, so they need the Instance on a public address with TLS. Self-hosted runners on your own network can use a private one.

  2. Pull the models your tests use into the Arsenal, at the Revisions they pin:

    hangar pull hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-bert --server-only
hangar pull sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 --revision <commit SHA> --server-only

    Mirrors keep the upstream Repo IDs and Commit SHAs, so tests pinned to a Commit SHA on huggingface.co work unchanged. If you would rather not list models up front, an admin can turn on Pull-through, so the first request for a model starts its Pull.

  3. Save a huggingface.co token as the Instance token for the huggingface Upstream (upstreams.huggingface.token, or HANGAR_UPSTREAMS_HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN), so the Instance's own Pulls count against an account rather than its IP address. If huggingface.co still answers 429, Hangar waits and tries again. A file that still fails after its retries leaves the Pull partial, with a Retry failed action.

  4. Create a read Token for CI under Settings, Tokens, limited to the Repos the tests use, and store it as a secret in your CI system, such as HANGAR_TOKEN in GitHub Actions.

docs.title: GitHub Actions example
docs.text:
name: Tests
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    env:
      HF_ENDPOINT: https://hangar.example.com
      HF_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HANGAR_TOKEN }}
      DISABLE_SAFETENSORS_CONVERSION: "1"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Restore the Hugging Face cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/huggingface/hub
          # models.txt lists the Repo IDs and Revisions the tests load,
          # so the cache changes when they do.
          key: hf-hub-${{ hashFiles('models.txt') }}
      - run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      - run: pytest

The libraries read HF_ENDPOINT and HF_TOKEN from the environment, so the tests need no changes. Restoring the cache still saves time when the Instance is close by, because nothing is downloaded at all. DISABLE_SAFETENSORS_CONVERSION stops transformers from trying the conversion service on huggingface.co for models that only have pickle weights; see Point HF_ENDPOINT at Hangar.

To download everything in one step and run the tests with no network requests, add a step before the tests and set HF_HUB_OFFLINE for them:

      - run: hf download sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 --revision <commit SHA>
      - run: pytest
        env:
          HF_HUB_OFFLINE: "1"

Pull requests from forks get no HANGAR_TOKEN. To let them download anyway, keep the models they need in public Repos and turn on anonymous reads (security.anonymous_read). Anyone who can reach the Instance can then read every public Repo, so weigh that against keeping fork jobs off the Instance.

docs.title: Other CI systems
docs.text: Any CI system works the same way: set HF_ENDPOINT to the Instance, HF_TOKEN to a Hangar Token from the system's secret store, and keep ~/.cache/huggingface/hub, or HF_HUB_CACHE if you set it, between runs if the system can.

docs.title: Errors you may see with Hangar
docs.text: Error Cause Fix "Repository Not Found for url" The Repo is not in the Arsenal, or the Token cannot read it. Private Repos answer as if they did not exist. Pull the Repo, and check the Token's scope and the Repos it is limited to. "Invalid credentials in Authorization header" HF_TOKEN holds a huggingface.co token (hf_...) rather than a Hangar Token (hgr_...), or the Token expired. Store a Hangar Token in the secret. HfHubHTTPError with status 409, naming a hangar pull command The Repo is a Partial mirror and the file was not pulled. Run the command it names, or pull the files the tests load. LocalEntryNotFoundError with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 The files are not in the restored cache. Download them in an earlier step, or change the cache key.

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Share one model cache across a team: the same idea for people and servers.
  • Python libraries and the hf CLI: HF_ENDPOINT with each client.
  • Permissions: Token scopes and limits.

docs.title: Collections
docs.text: A Collection is a named, ordered list of Repos that a User or Organisation curates, such as "Embedding models we support" or "Datasets for the March evaluation". Each item can have a note. A Collection can hold models, datasets and other Collections.

docs.title: Who can see and change a Collection
docs.text:
A Collection has its own visibility, which works like a Repo's:

Visibility Who can see it public (the default) Anyone signed in, and anonymous visitors if the Instance allows anonymous reads (security.anonymous_read). internal Any signed-in User. private Members of the Namespace that owns it, and Instance admins.

Each viewer sees only the items they can read: a private Repo in a public Collection stays hidden from people who cannot read the Repo.

To create or change a Collection in a Namespace, you need the write Role in it. Your personal Namespace is always yours, and Instance admins can change any Collection.

docs.title: In the web UI
docs.text:
1. Open Collections and select New Collection. Choose the Namespace, a title and the visibility.
  2. On the Collection's page, select Edit. Add a Repo by its ID, such as acme/bert-tiny, or datasets/acme/reviews for a dataset.
  3. Drag items by their handle to reorder them, or focus a handle and use the arrow keys, then press Space. Add a note to an item, and select Save note.
  4. Select Done.

A Repo's page lists the Collections it is in under In Collections. Deleting a Collection does not affect the Repos in it.

docs.title: With huggingface_hub
docs.text:
The Hub's collections API works against Hangar, so huggingface_hub can manage Collections. The compatibility suite tests each of these calls:

from huggingface_hub import HfApi

api = HfApi()  # HF_ENDPOINT and HF_TOKEN point at Hangar
c = api.create_collection("Embedding models", namespace="acme", private=True)
c = api.add_collection_item(c.slug, item_id="sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2", item_type="model", note="Default")
c = api.add_collection_item(c.slug, item_id="acme/reviews", item_type="dataset")
api.update_collection_item(c.slug, c.items[1].item_object_id, position=0, note="Evaluation set")
api.update_collection_metadata(c.slug, title="Embedding models we support")
for item in api.get_collection(c.slug).items:
    print(item.item_type, item.item_id, item.note)
api.list_collections(owner="acme")

private=True makes a private Collection. Adding an item that is already in the Collection fails, unless you pass exists_ok=True.

docs.title: With the native API
docs.text:
The web UI uses the native API's /api/hangar/v1/collections routes, which you can call with a Token:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer hgr_..." \
  "https://hangar.example.com/api/hangar/v1/collections?owner=acme"

The native API reference lists every route, including adding, moving and removing items.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Limit Value Title 60 characters. The Collection's address, its slug, comes from the title. Description 150 characters Note on an item 500 characters Items in a Collection 1,000

docs.title: Work with datasets
docs.text: Datasets are Repos of type dataset. In URLs and the CLI they carry a datasets/ prefix: datasets/acme/reviews.

docs.title: In the web UI
docs.text:
Datasets have their own section, Datasets in the top bar (/datasets), separate from Models: each list holds one type only, with its own filters and its own New dataset button. Old /arsenal links still work. They open the Models list, or the Datasets list for ?type=datasets.

A dataset can hold any files, not only training data: for example, sample inputs for another project's tests. When none of its files is a data file the Dataset Viewer reads (Parquet, CSV, JSON Lines, text, Arrow, WebDataset archives, or folders of images or audio), the Viewer tab says there is nothing to preview and links to the files, and Use this dataset shows the snippets that download the files: the hf CLI, huggingface_hub and git.

docs.title: Link models and datasets
docs.text:
Links are optional. A model names the datasets it was trained or evaluated on in its Model card's datasets metadata, as on the Hugging Face Hub:

---
datasets:
  - acme/reviews
  - imdb
---

To set it in the UI, open the model's Settings tab and use Datasets used: search the Arsenal by name, or type the ID of a dataset on an Upstream, then Commit to the Model card. Hangar keeps the card's other metadata and text. The model's sidebar then lists the datasets under Datasets used, and each dataset's sidebar lists the model under Used by. Mirrors keep their upstream card, so set it on the Upstream instead.

To group a project's models and datasets, put them in a Collection.

docs.title: Load them
docs.text:
With HF_ENDPOINT pointing at Hangar:

from datasets import load_dataset

ds = load_dataset("lhoestq/demo1", split="train")
stream = load_dataset("lhoestq/demo1", split="train", streaming=True)

pandas reads the hf:// file system that huggingface_hub provides:

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_parquet("hf://datasets/acme/reviews/data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet")

Polars has its own hf:// client, which always talks to huggingface.co and ignores HF_ENDPOINT. Open the files through huggingface_hub instead:

import polars as pl
from huggingface_hub import HfFileSystem

fs = HfFileSystem()
paths = fs.glob("datasets/acme/reviews/**/*.parquet")
df = pl.concat([pl.read_parquet(fs.open(p, "rb")) for p in paths])

DuckDB reads files over HTTPS from resolve URLs. Its own hf:// scheme talks to huggingface.co, so use HTTPS URLs for Hangar:

INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
CREATE SECRET hangar (TYPE http, EXTRA_HTTP_HEADERS MAP {'Authorization': 'Bearer hgr_...'});
SELECT count(*) FROM 'https://hangar.example.com/datasets/acme/reviews/resolve/refs%2Fconvert%2Fparquet/default/train/0000.parquet';

docs.title: The datasets-server name
docs.text: datasets asks datasets-server.<your host>/info about a dataset before loading it, with a long timeout. Hangar serves the Dataset Viewer API there, so create a DNS name datasets-server.hangar.example.com that points at Hangar (the Helm chart's Ingress adds it with ingress.datasetsServerHost: true), or make sure the name does not resolve. Without either, load_dataset can wait a long time before it starts.

docs.title: Configs and Splits
docs.text: A Config is a named subset of a dataset, from the card's configs: YAML or inferred from the file layout, and a Split is a part of a Config, such as train or test. hangar info datasets/acme/reviews lists them with row counts and sizes.

docs.title: Parquet export
docs.text:
Hangar converts every Config and Split to Parquet, on the refs/convert/parquet branch, as huggingface.co does. The Dataset Viewer reads it, and you can load it directly.

A Mirror keeps the Upstream's own Parquet export instead of converting. A Pull of the dataset's files does not always bring the export's files with it; until they are in the Arsenal, the Viewer tab says to pull them, which hangar pull datasets/<namespace>/<name> --parquet-only --server-only does.

docs.title: Partial and Parquet-only Pulls
docs.text:
Pull only the Configs and Splits you need, or only their Parquet export, which can turn a very large raw dataset into a few GB:

hangar pull datasets/HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu --config sample-10BT --split train --parquet-only --to ./fineweb

In the UI, open a dataset in Discover and choose Configs, Splits and Parquet export only before Pull into arsenal.

docs.title: The Dataset Viewer
docs.text: The Viewer tab of a dataset previews rows, searches and filters them, and shows statistics for each column, through an API compatible with the Hub's Dataset Viewer at <public_url>/datasets-server/.... Until a Split is converted, it shows "Preparing preview".

docs.title: Pulling gated models from huggingface.co
docs.text:
Gated and private Repos on huggingface.co need a token from an account that has access.

  1. On huggingface.co, accept the model's conditions and create a read token.
  2. In Hangar, open Settings, Upstream tokens, and save it for huggingface.

Pulls you start then use your token. Hangar encrypts saved tokens with the Instance key and never shows them again. An admin can also set an Instance token for an Upstream (upstreams.<id>.token), which Pulls use when the user has none.

docs.title: Gating your own Repos
docs.text:
An admin of a Repo can require people to ask for access under the Repo's Settings:

  • Automatic accepts every request straight away, after the person fills in the form.
  • Manual queues requests for an admin to accept or reject under Settings, Access requests.

The Settings tab also takes a message to show people asking for access. To add fields to the request form, such as a company name, a country or a checkbox to accept terms, set gating.fields with the native API. Field types are text, checkbox, country, date and select:

curl -X PATCH https://hangar.example.com/api/hangar/v1/repos/models/acme/my-model \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer hgr_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"gating": {"fields": [{"name": "Company", "type": "text", "required": true},
                            {"name": "I accept the terms", "type": "checkbox", "required": true}]}}'

Saving gating in the Settings tab keeps the fields. Gating works through the Hub API too: huggingface_hub raises GatedRepoError until access is granted, as it does on huggingface.co.

docs.title: Use git and git-lfs
docs.text:
Every Repo is a git repository over HTTPS, at the same URL as on the Hub plus .git:

git clone https://hangar.example.com/acme/my-model.git
git clone https://hangar.example.com/datasets/acme/reviews.git

Install git-lfs first (git lfs install), so large files download as content rather than pointers. git 2.39 or later is supported.

docs.title: Sign in
docs.text:
Use any username and a Token as the password. A credential helper keeps it:

git config --global credential.helper store   # or osxkeychain, manager, libsecret
git clone https://hangar.example.com/acme/private-model.git
# Username: anything, such as your username
# Password: hgr_...

A private Repo you cannot read answers as if it did not exist, so check the Token if a clone says the Repo was not found.

docs.title: Partial and shallow clones
docs.text:
git clone --depth 1 https://hangar.example.com/acme/my-model.git
GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 git clone https://hangar.example.com/acme/my-model.git
cd my-model && git lfs pull --include "*.safetensors"

docs.title: Push
docs.text:
git lfs track "*.safetensors" "*.gguf"
git add .gitattributes model.safetensors
git commit -m "Add weights"
git push

Repos created through the Hub API start with a .gitattributes that already tracks the usual weight and archive types with LFS. Non-LFS files over git.max_blob_size (10 MiB by default) are refused, with a message that tells you to track them with LFS.

Commits pushed with git and Commits made through the Hub API are the same Commits, with the same SHAs.

Rules for pushes:

  • Force-pushes to a Repo's default branch are refused unless git.allow_force_push is on. Admins of the Repo can always force-push, with any Token that can push: the User whose personal Namespace holds it, admin Members of its Organisation, and Instance admins. Force-pushes to other branches are allowed.
  • Mirrors are read-only, so pushes to them are refused. Detach a Mirror first to make it an ordinary Repo.
  • If two pushes to the same branch race, one wins and the other gets git's usual non-fast-forward rejection.
  • git push --atomic fails with "the receiving end does not support --atomic push", because Hangar does not advertise the capability. Every push is applied all or nothing anyway, so push without --atomic.
  • A push may update at most 10,000 branches and tags, and no object in it may be larger than 64 MiB (or git.max_blob_size, if that is larger) when unpacked.
  • A Commit may hold at most 1,000,000 files and folders, and no path may be longer than 4,096 bytes.
  • Names that a client could check out as .git (such as .GIT or git~1), the names . and .., and names with a backslash are refused.

docs.title: The hangar CLI
docs.text: hangar is one binary for the server and the client. Install it as Binary describes. Every command is in the CLI reference.

docs.title: Sign in
docs.text:
hangar login --url https://hangar.example.com     # device sign-in in your browser
hangar login --url https://hangar.example.com --token hgr_...
hangar whoami
hangar logout

The device sign-in opens the Instance's Connect a device page. Type the code the CLI prints, check the client (hangar-cli), the time and the IP address, and choose read access, or write if you will push, upload or pull into the Instance. The Token expires in 30 days; run hangar login again then.

The URL and username are saved in ~/.config/hangar/config.yaml; the Token goes in the OS keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or the Secret Service on Linux) where one is available, otherwise in that file with mode 0600. In scripts and CI, set HANGAR_CLI_URL and HANGAR_CLI_TOKEN instead, or pass --url and --token. HANGAR_CLI_CONFIG points the CLI at another configuration file, and HANGAR_CLI_NO_KEYCHAIN=1 keeps the Token in that file instead of the OS keychain.

docs.title: Turn on tab completion
docs.text:
hangar completion <shell> prints a completion script for bash, zsh, fish or PowerShell. The Homebrew cask installs the bash, zsh and fish scripts for you, and each release archive has all four in its completions folder. To load the script yourself, add a line to your shell's startup file:

source <(hangar completion bash)    # ~/.bashrc; needs the bash-completion package
source <(hangar completion zsh)     # ~/.zshrc, after compinit
hangar completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/hangar.fish

In PowerShell, add hangar completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression to your profile.

Besides commands and flags, Tab completes:

  • Repo IDs from the Arsenal and, after a colon, the Repo's quants, as in hangar pull bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M.
  • The IDs of your Jobs that have not finished, for hangar jobs watch and hangar jobs cancel.
  • A dataset's Configs and Splits, for hangar pull --config and --split.
  • Flag values with a fixed set of choices, such as --type and --sort, the keys of hangar search --filter, and the configuration keys of --set.
  • Folder names, for flags and arguments that take a folder.

Completions that need the Instance use the saved login, or --url and --token when they come earlier on the command line. If the Instance does not answer within 3 seconds, Tab offers nothing.

docs.title: Find and inspect
docs.text:
hangar search llama --filter format=gguf --filter quant=Q4_K_M   # the Arsenal
hangar search qwen --upstream --filter gguf --sort downloads     # Discover on huggingface.co
hangar info bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF                 # files, quants, Dependencies, Arsenal state
hangar info datasets/lhoestq/demo1                               # Configs, Splits, rows and sizes

docs.title: Pull and download
docs.text:
hangar pull bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M
hangar pull hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-bert --include '*.json' --include '*.safetensors'
hangar pull Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --server-only
hangar pull datasets/lhoestq/demo1 --to ./demo1

If the files are not in the Arsenal, hangar pull asks the Instance to pull them and shows the progress, then downloads them into the Hugging Face cache ($HF_HUB_CACHE, default ~/.cache/huggingface/hub), in the same layout Python libraries use, so they reuse the files and so does the CLI. Downloads resume after an interruption, retry by themselves after a dropped connection or a busy proxy, and are checked against their SHA-256 or git object ID.

docs.title: Upload and import
docs.text:
hangar push ./my-finetune acme/my-finetune --create --private
hangar import --from-hf-cache

See Uploading and Importing an existing cache.

docs.title: Local tools
docs.text:
eval "$(hangar env)"                                          # HF_ENDPOINT and HF_TOKEN for Python tools
hangar lmstudio install bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M
hangar ollama install bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text:
hangar jobs list
hangar jobs watch <job-id>
hangar jobs cancel <job-id>

docs.title: Scripting
docs.text: Every command takes --json and prints JSON on standard output; progress goes to standard error. hangar server and hangar worker print only logs, so for them --json selects JSON logs, which is also the default. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 2 usage error, 3 not found, 4 authentication error.

docs.title: Use the hf CLI
docs.text:
The hf CLI that comes with huggingface_hub works against Hangar with HF_ENDPOINT. The compatibility suite runs hf auth login, hf auth whoami, hf repos create, hf upload and hf download against Hangar on every pull request.

export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hangar.example.com
hf auth login --token hgr_...
hf auth whoami
hf download hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-bert --include "*.json"
hf repos create acme/my-model --private
hf upload acme/my-model ./weights

docs.title: Sign in
docs.text:
Use hf auth login --token, or the HF_TOKEN variable. The browser sign-in that hf auth login starts without --token also works: open Hangar's device page, type the code your terminal shows, check which client asked, when and from which IP address, and choose read or write access. Hangar then creates a Token for the CLI that expires in 30 days. Choose write if you will upload. Hangar never fills in the code from a link, so a link someone sends you cannot sign their device in as you.

hf keeps one active Token in ~/.cache/huggingface/token, whichever endpoint it came from. If you also use huggingface.co, set HF_ENDPOINT and HF_TOKEN in each shell instead of signing in to both:

HF_ENDPOINT=https://hangar.example.com HF_TOKEN=hgr_... hf auth whoami

eval "$(hangar env)" sets both for the Instance you signed in to with hangar login.

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
hf download acme/my-model                              # every file, into the Hugging Face cache
hf download acme/my-model config.json                  # one file
hf download acme/my-model --include "*.safetensors"    # files that match
hf download acme/my-model --revision dev               # a branch, a tag or a Commit SHA
hf download acme/my-model --local-dir ./my-model       # into a folder instead of the cache
hf download acme/reviews --repo-type dataset           # a dataset Repo

Mirrors keep the upstream Repo IDs and Commit SHAs, so the same commands and Revisions work against Hangar and huggingface.co. If a Repo is not in the Arsenal yet, pull it first with hangar pull or from Discover.

docs.title: Upload
docs.text:
hf repos create acme/my-model --private
hf upload acme/my-model ./weights .                            # a folder, as one Commit
hf upload acme/my-model ./weights . --commit-message "Add weights"
hf upload acme/my-model ./config.json copy/config.json --revision dev

Uploading to a branch that does not exist yet creates it. With hf_xet installed, large files go up as Xet uploads, which Hangar accepts with no setup. Every upload is a real Commit, the same as one made with git; see Uploading.

docs.title: Errors you may see
docs.text:
Error Cause Fix "Invalid credentials in Authorization header" The Token is wrong, expired or revoked, or it is a huggingface.co token (hf_...) rather than a Hangar one (hgr_...). Create a Token in Hangar under Settings, Tokens. hf auth whoami shows your huggingface.co account HF_ENDPOINT is not set in this shell. Export HF_ENDPOINT, or use eval "$(hangar env)". "Repository Not Found for url" The Repo is private and your Token cannot read it, or it is not in the Arsenal. Private Repos answer as if they did not exist. Check the Token, and pull the Repo first. HTTP 409, saying the file is not in the arsenal The Repo is a Partial mirror and the file was not pulled. Download only the files it holds with --include, or run the hangar pull command it names.

See also Python libraries and Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Import an existing cache
docs.text: hangar import adds models you already have on disk to the Arsenal without downloading them again. Uploads go through the Instance's API, so it works against any Hangar you can write to. A file that fails to upload does not stop the import: the other files of the same Repo still go up and are added to its Mirror, the other Repos are imported, and the results name what failed. Run the same command again to send only what failed.

docs.title: A Hugging Face cache
docs.text:
hangar import --from-hf-cache                     # ~/.cache/huggingface/hub, or $HF_HUB_CACHE
hangar import --from-hf-cache /mnt/models/hub

For each Repo in the cache, Hangar creates a Mirror of the huggingface.co Repo with the same ID at the cached Commit: the snapshot that main points at, or the newest snapshot if the cache does not record main. The Instance fetches the history, which is small, and the CLI uploads only the cached large files that the Mirror is missing. Files you have not cached show as Not in arsenal, and you can pull them later.

The import reads every cached snapshot of a Repo, not only that one, and matches files by content rather than by name: the SHA-256 of large files and the git blob ID of the others. A file counts as matched when the Mirror has the same content at the cached Commit, the default branch or the Commit of any other cached snapshot, under any path.

If the Repo is already a Mirror, the import fills in the files it is missing. When the cached Commit is newer than the Mirror's last sync, Hangar fetches its history first. The uploaded files are added to the Mirror at the Commit they matched, so files that have changed on huggingface.co since are not downloaded again.

With --offline, or for a Repo huggingface.co does not have, each Repo becomes a local Repo with one Commit of the cached files instead, from the snapshot of main or else the newest. Add --namespace to put those in a Namespace of your choice. An import never commits to a Mirror, because Mirrors are read-only.

docs.title: Files that do not match
docs.text:
A file whose content matches nothing in the Mirror is not uploaded. The results count it as not matched, then name it with the reason:

Not matched:
  acme/model: notes.safetensors (snapshot 1a2b3c4d5e6f): no file in the Mirror at Commits 9f8e7d6c5b4a or 0c1d2e3f4a5b has this content
  acme/model: model.safetensors: its content differs from model.safetensors at Commit 9f8e7d6c5b4a and from every other file checked

The snapshot is named when the Repo has more than one in the cache. With --json, each result lists these files under not_matched, with path, reason and snapshot.

docs.title: A folder
docs.text:
hangar import --from-dir ./weights --repo acme/my-model

This is the same as hangar push ./weights acme/my-model --create.

docs.title: LM Studio
docs.text:
hangar import --from-lmstudio
hangar import --from-lmstudio ~/lm-models

Each <publisher>/<repo> folder that matches a huggingface.co Repo of the same name becomes a Partial mirror holding the files whose content matches a file of the Mirror's default branch, whatever their names. Files that match nothing are reported as not matched, with the reason. Other folders become local Repos.

docs.title: Ollama
docs.text:
hangar import --from-ollama --namespace acme

Each model and tag in Ollama's store (~/.ollama/models, or $OLLAMA_MODELS) becomes a local Repo, such as acme/llama3.2 for llama3.2:latest and acme/llama3.2-1b for llama3.2:1b, with the GGUF file and Ollama's template, system, params and LICENSE files. Hangar's Ollama endpoint then serves it back with the same template.

docs.title: Choose which models
docs.text:
By default, a source imports every model it holds. To import only some, give --only once for each model, as the source names it:

hangar import --from-hf-cache --only Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct --only 'bartowski/*'
hangar import --from-lmstudio --only lmstudio-community/gemma-3-12b-it-GGUF
hangar import --from-ollama --only llama3.2:1b --only 'qwen3:*'
  • For a Hugging Face cache, give the Repo ID. Datasets start with datasets/, such as datasets/acme/data.
  • For LM Studio, give the <publisher>/<repo> folder, or the Repo ID it becomes.
  • For Ollama, give the model and tag as ollama list shows them. A model without a tag means :latest, as in Ollama, so use llama3.2:* for every tag.

Patterns can use * and ?, which do not match /, and ignore case. If a pattern matches nothing, the import stops before it uploads anything and names the pattern, so a typo does not leave a model out. --only does not apply to --from-dir.

docs.title: Symbolic links
docs.text: Every source follows symbolic links only to files inside the folder it reads, or to files in a Hugging Face cache. Other links are skipped and named on stderr, as hangar push does.

docs.title: Check first
docs.text: Every source takes --dry-run, which lists what would be imported, and --json.

docs.title: Load models in Kubernetes without downloading them on every Pod start
docs.text:
A Pod that loads a model with huggingface_hub, such as a vLLM server or a transformers job, downloads it into the container's Hugging Face cache when it starts. The cache lives in the container's own file system, so a restarted, rescheduled or new Pod downloads the whole model again from huggingface.co. With large models and several replicas, that makes starts slow and can reach huggingface.co's rate limits.

Three changes fix it, and each works without the others:

  1. Serve the models from a Hangar Instance on your own network, so downloads do not go to huggingface.co.
  2. Keep the Hugging Face cache on a volume, so a restarted Pod finds the files it downloaded before.
  3. Download before the server starts, in an init container, and load with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, so the server starts only with every file present and makes no requests.

The examples use vLLM. Any image that loads models with huggingface_hub works the same way.

docs.title: 1. Serve the models from Hangar
docs.text:
Run Hangar in the cluster with the Helm chart, or anywhere the Pods can reach. Then pull the models into the Arsenal. Pull whole Repos: servers read the config and tokenizer files as well as the weights, and a file that is not present fails the load.

hangar pull Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --server-only

Create a read Token for the Pods under Settings, Tokens, limited to the Repos they serve, and keep it in a Secret:

kubectl create secret generic hangar-token --from-literal=token=hgr_...

Point the Pods at the Instance:

env:
  - name: HF_ENDPOINT
    value: https://hangar.example.com
  - name: HF_TOKEN
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef: {name: hangar-token, key: token}

Use the Instance's public URL (server.public_url) as HF_ENDPOINT, even from inside the cluster: Hangar builds some links it sends to clients from it, such as the next page of a long file listing. Mirrors keep the upstream Commit SHAs, so a --revision pinned on huggingface.co works unchanged.

Now huggingface.co sees one download per file, from Hangar's Pull, however many Pods start. On S3 storage in redirect mode, Pods download from presigned URLs of the bucket, so they must be able to reach its endpoint; otherwise use proxy mode (storage.s3.download_mode). See Storage backends.

docs.title: 2. Keep the cache on a volume
docs.text:
Mount a PersistentVolumeClaim and point the Hugging Face cache at it with HF_HOME. The cache is then $HF_HOME/hub, whatever the image's home folder:

env:
  - name: HF_HOME
    value: /models
volumeMounts:
  - name: models
    mountPath: /models

A restarted Pod that gets the same volume loads from it instead of downloading again. huggingface_hub still asks the Instance whether the branch has a newer Commit; step 3 removes those requests.

How you give each replica a volume depends on your storage:

  • For one replica, use a ReadWriteOnce claim, as in the example below.
  • For several replicas that each keep their own copy, use a StatefulSet with volumeClaimTemplates, so each Pod keeps its own volume across restarts.
  • For several replicas that share one copy, use a ReadWriteMany claim, if your storage class supports it. Fill it once, for example from a Job that runs the init container below, and mount it read-only in the serving Pods.

docs.title: 3. Download in an init container
docs.text:
The Hangar container image includes the hangar CLI, and hangar pull downloads a Repo into a Hugging Face cache in the layout huggingface_hub reads. Run it in an init container, then start the server with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1:

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: models
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 20Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: vllm
spec:
  replicas: 1
  strategy:
    type: Recreate   # the new Pod needs the volume the old one holds
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app: vllm}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app: vllm}
    spec:
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 65532   # the group the Hangar image runs as, so it can write to the volume
      initContainers:
        - name: download-model
          image: ghcr.io/hangar-hub/hangar:latest
          args: ["pull", "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "--cache-dir", "/models/hub"]
          env:
            - name: HANGAR_CLI_URL
              value: https://hangar.example.com
            - name: HANGAR_CLI_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef: {name: hangar-token, key: token}
          volumeMounts:
            - name: models
              mountPath: /models
      containers:
        - name: vllm
          image: vllm/vllm-openai:latest
          args: ["--model", "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"]
          env:
            - name: HF_HOME
              value: /models
            - name: HF_HUB_OFFLINE
              value: "1"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: models
              mountPath: /models
      volumes:
        - name: models
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: models
  • On the first start, hangar pull downloads every file of the Repo. The cache names each file by its hash, so on later starts it downloads only files whose content is not on the volume yet, such as those of a new Revision.
  • hangar pull checks each download against its SHA-256 or git object ID, and resumes an interrupted one, so a Pod killed part-way through finishes the download on its next start.
  • With a read Token, the Repo must already be in the Arsenal: starting a Pull needs a write Token. If it is not there, the init container fails and the Pod does not start, which is safer than a server that starts without its model.
  • To pin a Revision, add --revision <commit SHA> to both hangar pull and vllm.
  • The init container asks the Instance which files the Repo has on every start, so a Pod starts only while the Instance is up. The server container needs no Token and makes no requests.

If you would rather not use the Hangar image, run hf download Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B in an init container from any image with huggingface_hub installed, with HF_ENDPOINT, HF_TOKEN and HF_HOME set as in the earlier steps.

docs.title: Errors you may see
docs.text: Error Cause Fix The init container fails with exit code 4 The Token is missing, wrong or expired. Check the Secret, and create a new Token if needed. The init container fails with "Permission denied" writing to /models The Hangar image runs as user and group 65532, and the volume is not writable by that group. Set fsGroup: 65532, as in the example, or prepare the volume's ownership another way. LocalEntryNotFoundError in the server with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 The files are not in the cache the server reads. Check that --cache-dir is $HF_HOME/hub, and that the model name and Revision match. RepositoryNotFoundError, "Repository Not Found for url" Without HF_HUB_OFFLINE, the Repo is not in the Arsenal or the Token cannot read it. Pull the Repo, and check the Token. A new Pod stays ContainerCreating with a Multi-Attach error event A ReadWriteOnce volume is still attached to the old Pod on another node. Use the Recreate strategy, a StatefulSet, or a ReadWriteMany volume.

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• vLLM: serve models with vLLM from Hangar, in a container or on a host.
  • Run Hangar on Kubernetes with Helm: put the Instance in the same cluster.
  • Share one model cache across a team: the same idea for people and servers outside Kubernetes.
  • The hangar CLI: hangar pull and its flags.

docs.title: Use LM Studio
docs.text:
LM Studio reads models from a folder laid out as <publisher>/<repo>/<files>. hangar lmstudio install downloads a model into your local Hugging Face cache and links it into that folder:

hangar lmstudio install bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M
hangar lmstudio install mlx-community/SmolLM-135M-Instruct-4bit
  • For a GGUF Repo, it installs one quant group and any mmproj-*.gguf projector; without a quant it picks Q4_K_M, or the closest one available.
  • MLX and other Repos are installed whole.
  • Files are symbolic links into the cache on macOS and Linux, so the disk is used once even when Python libraries use the same model. Use --link-mode hardlink or --link-mode copy if LM Studio's folder is on another disk, or on Windows (where the default is hardlink).

Restart LM Studio, or open My Models, to see them.

docs.title: Where the models folder is
docs.text:
In order:

  1. --lmstudio-dir, if you give it.
  2. The downloadsFolder setting in settings.json in LM Studio's home folder. The home folder is the path in ~/.lmstudio-home-pointer if that file exists, otherwise ~/.cache/lm-studio if it exists, otherwise ~/.lmstudio. This is how LM Studio itself finds its home.
  3. models in that home folder.

docs.title: Keep track
docs.text:
hangar lmstudio list            # what is installed, and whether a newer Revision exists
hangar lmstudio remove bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF
hangar lmstudio remove bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF --prune   # also free the cache

The CLI records installs in ~/.config/hangar/lmstudio.json. --prune deletes the model's cached files unless another install uses them; Python code that used the same cached files downloads them again next time.

To add models you already have in LM Studio to the Arsenal, see Importing an existing cache.

docs.title: Run a private Ollama registry
docs.text:
Hangar serves every GGUF Repo in its Arsenal as an Ollama registry. Ollama installs on your network pull from it by name, the same way they pull from huggingface.co, and the files stay on your own storage. There is no Modelfile to write and no separate registry to run.

This guide sets up the registry for a team or a fleet of Ollama servers. For pulling one model to your own machine, see Ollama.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
An Ollama model name can start with a registry host. For a name such as hangar.example.com/bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M, Ollama asks hangar.example.com for the manifest of the Q4_K_M tag of bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF. Hangar builds the manifest from the Repo when Ollama asks for it:

  • The model layer is the GGUF file for the quant the tag names, served from the Blob store without a copy.
  • The chat template comes from the Repo's template file, or is matched from the GGUF file's own chat template.
  • system, params and LICENSE files in the Repo become the system prompt, parameters and licence.
  • A matching mmproj-*.gguf projector is included for vision models.

Every GGUF Repo works this way: Mirrors of huggingface.co Repos, Repos you uploaded, and models you imported from Ollama.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A running Instance. See Get started.
  • A host name for Hangar that every Ollama install can reach. Ollama asks for the registry at the root of the host, so serve Hangar at the root of its own host name, not under a path such as example.com/hangar/.
  • HTTPS with a certificate the Ollama machines trust, which TLS and reverse proxies describes. Ollama uses HTTPS unless you pass --insecure.

docs.title: 1. Fill the registry
docs.text:
Pull the quants you want to offer from huggingface.co. --server-only puts them in the Arsenal without downloading them to your machine:

hangar pull bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M --server-only
hangar pull bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q8_0 --server-only

Each Pull keeps only the quants you chose, as a Partial mirror. To follow new upstream Commits of the same quant, add --track.

To serve a GGUF model that is not on any Upstream, such as your own fine-tune, upload it to a Repo with its template, system and params files if it has them:

hangar push ./my-finetune-gguf acme/support-assistant-GGUF --create --private

To move models you already have in Ollama into the registry, import them. Each model and tag becomes a Repo in the Namespace you name:

hangar import --from-ollama --namespace acme

See Uploading and Importing an existing cache.

docs.title: 2. Decide who can pull
docs.text: Ollama signs every registry request with the key pair in the .ollama folder of the user that runs the Ollama server. Hangar reads Repos for a key only after someone registers it. Choose one of these ways.

docs.title: A key for each person
docs.text: Each person registers their own key with hangar ollama key register, or pastes ~/.ollama/id_ed25519.pub under Settings, Ollama keys. Their Ollama then reads what they can read, private Repos included.

docs.title: A key for each Ollama server
docs.text:
For a shared Ollama server, create a User for it, give that User read in the Organisations whose models it serves, sign in as it and paste the server's public key under Settings, Ollama keys. A key pasted in Settings reads every Repo its User can read, so keep that User's access narrow.

For the official ollama/ollama container image, the server runs as root, so its key is /root/.ollama/id_ed25519.pub inside the container:

docker exec ollama cat /root/.ollama/id_ed25519.pub

Keep /root/.ollama on a volume, as Ollama's own instructions do, so the key survives a new container and stays registered.

docs.title: No key
docs.text: If the models are public Repos and the Instance allows anonymous reads (security.anonymous_read, off by default), Ollama pulls them without a key. Anyone who can reach the Instance can then read every public Repo, so use this only on a network you trust.

docs.title: 3. Pull from Ollama
docs.text:
On each machine, pull with the registry host in front of the Repo ID and the quant as the tag:

ollama pull hangar.example.com/bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M
ollama run hangar.example.com/bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M
  • The tag picks a quant, ignoring case, or a full GGUF filename. Without a tag, Ollama asks for latest, and Hangar serves Q4_K_M if the Repo has it, otherwise the closest quant.
  • For an Ollama server in a container, run the same command inside it, such as docker exec ollama ollama pull hangar.example.com/....
  • To give the model a shorter name on one machine, copy it with ollama cp, such as ollama cp hangar.example.com/acme/support-assistant-GGUF:Q4_K_M support.

On a plain-HTTP Instance on your own network, add --insecure to ollama pull. hangar ollama install runs ollama pull for you and adds --insecure for http:// Instances. It also checks that the quant is in the Arsenal and that your key is registered first; see Install with the hangar CLI.

docs.title: Keep the registry up to date
docs.text:
• A tracking Mirror checks its upstream branch every six hours by default and pulls new versions of the quants it holds. Ollama gets the new file the next time it pulls the same name.
  • To let people pull other quants of a Repo the registry already mirrors, an admin can turn on Pull-through. A request for a quant the Mirror does not hold then starts its Pull, and ollama pull asks you to try again when it finishes. A Repo that is not in the Arsenal at all still needs a Pull first.
  • To keep large Pulls off your connection during working hours, see Pull windows and bandwidth.

docs.title: Errors you may see
docs.text: Problem Cause Fix ollama pull fails with file does not exist The quant is not in the Arsenal. Ollama does not show the message Hangar sends with it, which names the Pull to run. Pull the quant with hangar pull <repo>:<quant> --server-only, or use hangar ollama install, which checks first. A private Repo fails to pull on one machine but works on another Hangar does not know the key of the Ollama server that sent the request, or that key's User cannot read the Repo. Hangar answers a Repo you cannot read as if it did not exist. Register the key of the machine that runs ollama serve, not only the one you type commands on, and check the User's Role. A gated Repo fails to pull The key's User has not been granted access. Request access to the Repo in Hangar. See Gated models. A TLS or certificate error Ollama uses HTTPS, and the Instance has no certificate the machine trusts. Set up TLS, or add --insecure on a network you trust.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• ollama push to Hangar is not supported. Upload with hangar push, hf upload or git, or use hangar import --from-ollama.
  • Ollama loads one GGUF file per model, so Hangar does not serve a quant split into several files (*-00001-of-0000N.gguf), and says so in its answer.
  • Ollama refuses redirects to other hosts, so Hangar streams Ollama downloads itself, even on S3 storage in redirect mode.
  • Hangar's CI tests the registry with Ollama 0.31.1; see Tested versions and platforms.

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Ollama: pull one model to your own machine.
  • Permissions: Ollama keys, Tokens and Roles.
  • Mirrors and Upstreams: Partial mirrors, tracking and Pull-through.

docs.title: Use Ollama
docs.text:
This guide pulls GGUF models from Hangar into Ollama on your own machine. To set Hangar up as the Ollama registry for a team or for shared Ollama servers, see Run a private Ollama registry.

Hangar serves GGUF Repos to Ollama the way huggingface.co does. Ollama signs its requests with the key pair in ~/.ollama, and Hangar needs that key for every Repo unless the Repo is public and the Instance allows anonymous reads (security.anonymous_read, off by default). Register the key once:

hangar ollama key register

or paste ~/.ollama/id_ed25519.pub under Settings, Ollama keys. To prove the key is yours, Settings shows an ssh-keygen -Y sign command to run on the machine that has the key; paste its output as the signature. The CLI signs with ~/.ollama/id_ed25519 itself. The private key never leaves your machine. A key you paste in Settings reads every Repo you can read. A key the CLI registers is tied to the CLI's token: it reads only what that token can read, and stops working when the token expires or is revoked. Run hangar ollama key register again after you sign the CLI in with a new token. Then this works with no Modelfile:

ollama pull hangar.example.com/bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M
ollama run hangar.example.com/bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M
  • The tag after : picks a quant, case-insensitively, or a full GGUF file name. Without a tag (Ollama's latest), Hangar picks Q4_K_M if the Repo has it, otherwise the closest quant.
  • The chat template comes from the Repo's template file, or is matched from the GGUF's own chat template. system, params and LICENSE files in the Repo become the system prompt, parameters and licence.
  • A matching mmproj-*.gguf projector is included for vision models.
  • The quant must be in the Arsenal. For a Partial mirror without it, ollama pull fails with file does not exist: Ollama does not show the message Hangar sends with it, which names the Pull to run. Pull the quant first with hangar pull <repo>:<quant> --server-only, or use hangar ollama install, which checks for you. If an admin turned on Pull-through, the request starts the Pull and ollama pull asks you to try again when it finishes.

docs.title: Install with the hangar CLI
docs.text:
hangar ollama install runs ollama pull for you, after two checks:

hangar ollama install bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M

  1. It checks that the quant is in the Arsenal. Without a quant, it checks the one Ollama asks for as latest. If the quant is missing, it says so, prints the command that pulls it into the Instance, and asks whether to run it:

    bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M is not in the Arsenal, so Ollama would fail with "file does not exist". Pull it into the Instance first:
  hangar pull bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M --server-only
Pull it now? [y/N]

    Answer y to pull it and continue. Any other answer stops with exit code 3 and leaves the command for you to run. To pull without the question, add --pull.

  2. It checks that your Ollama key is registered and offers to register it. Add --yes to register it without the question.

A quant the Repo does not have stops the command with the list of quants it does have.

docs.title: HTTPS or HTTP
docs.text:
Ollama uses HTTPS unless you pass --insecure. Use HTTPS with a trusted certificate (see TLS and reverse proxies), or for a plain-HTTP Instance on your network:

ollama pull --insecure hangar.lan:8080/bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M

hangar ollama install adds --insecure for http:// Instances.

docs.title: Private Repos
docs.text: With your key registered, Hangar gives Ollama a short-lived token for each Repo you can read, private Repos included.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• ollama push to Hangar is not supported. Use hangar import --from-ollama to bring models you have in Ollama into the Arsenal.
  • Ollama must reach Hangar on the host the model name gives, at the root of that host.
  • On S3 in redirect mode, Hangar answers a model layer download with a redirect to a presigned URL, so ollama pull takes the bytes straight from the bucket, as hf download does. Ollama follows that redirect only to a public address unless you pass --insecure, so with a bucket on a private network, such as MinIO on your LAN, pull with --insecure or set storage.s3.download_mode: proxy.

docs.title: Pull windows and bandwidth
docs.text:
Pulls are queued and resumable, and you can limit their rate, so a large Pull does not have to saturate a home connection. Set these in the configuration (or HANGAR_PULL_* variables):

pull:
  bandwidth_limit: 20MiB     # bytes per second across the whole Instance; 0 means no limit
  concurrency: 4             # files transferring at once across the Instance
  windows: ["01:00-07:00"]   # only start file transfers in these windows
server:
  timezone: Europe/London    # the time zone windows are in
  • The bandwidth limit holds across every worker: each worker leases a share of the budget from the database every few seconds.
  • Outside a window, Pulls are planned straight away (so the history is browsable) but file transfers wait. Transfers already running finish their current part, then wait. The UI shows "Waiting for pull window (01:00-07:00)".
  • Windows can span midnight, such as 22:00-06:00.
  • A user with write can start a Pull outside the windows with hangar pull --now, which still keeps to the bandwidth limit, while the Instance setting Let writers pull now (pull.allow_override_windows, under Admin, Pull settings) is on, as it is by default.
  • Admins can also change the bandwidth limit, concurrency and windows under Admin, Pull settings.

Time spent waiting for the bandwidth limit is exported as the hangar.pull.rate_limited.duration metric.

docs.title: Use Hangar from Python
docs.text:
Every library built on huggingface_hub works against Hangar once HF_ENDPOINT points at it:

export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hangar.example.com
export HF_TOKEN=hgr_...
export DISABLE_SAFETENSORS_CONVERSION=1

(eval "$(hangar env)" sets all three.) The compatibility suite runs huggingface_hub, transformers, sentence-transformers and datasets against Hangar on every pull request, and diffusers nightly. Tested versions and platforms lists the versions, and the compatibility matrix lists every Hub endpoint and its status.

docs.title: huggingface_hub
docs.text:
from huggingface_hub import HfApi, hf_hub_download, snapshot_download

api = HfApi()
info = api.model_info("bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF")
path = hf_hub_download("hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-bert", "config.json")
folder = snapshot_download("hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-bert", allow_patterns=["*.json", "*.safetensors"])

Revisions work as on the Hub: a branch, a tag, a Commit SHA or refs/pr/1. Downloads resume after an interruption, and with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 everything already in the cache loads with no network.

docs.title: transformers and sentence-transformers
docs.text:
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-bert")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-bert")
encoder = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")

Models with remote code (trust_remote_code=True) load offline as soon as their Pull finishes, because Hangar pulls the code Dependencies they name in auto_map first.

docs.title: diffusers
docs.text:
from diffusers import DiffusionPipeline

pipe = DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained("hf-internal-testing/tiny-stable-diffusion-torch")

docs.title: Files that are not in the Arsenal
docs.text:
A Partial mirror lists every file of the Repo with its size, but holds only the files that were pulled. Downloading a file it does not hold fails with HTTP 409 and the error code EntryNotFound, which huggingface_hub raises as RemoteEntryNotFoundError. The message names the hangar pull command that gets the file.

snapshot_download stops at the first such file, so pass allow_patterns to download only the files the mirror holds:

from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

folder = snapshot_download("bartowski/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-GGUF", allow_patterns=["*Q4_K_M.gguf", "*.json", "*.md"])

With the hf CLI, use --include in the same way. To get a missing file, pull it with hangar pull <repo> --include <file> or from the Repo page.

If the admin turned on Pull-through, a download of a file that is not held starts the file's Pull instead and streams the file as it arrives. Ranged requests, such as a resumed download, work too: they wait until the transfer reaches the start of the range.

docs.title: Large downloads
docs.text: On S3 storage in redirect mode, downloads go straight to presigned URLs, so file bytes do not pass through Hangar. huggingface_hub refuses plain HTTP downloads over 50 GB when it knows the size; Hangar serves files over 50 GB in redirect mode in a way the client accepts. In proxy mode and on the filesystem Blob store, download files over 50 GB with hangar pull or git lfs instead.

docs.title: Share one Hugging Face model cache across a team
docs.text:
Every machine that runs huggingface_hub, transformers or the hf CLI keeps its own cache, by default in ~/.cache/huggingface/hub. On a team, that means each person and each server downloads the same multi-gigabyte models from huggingface.co, and each copy takes up its own disk space.

You can keep one copy for everyone in two ways: put the cache folder itself on shared storage, or run Hangar as the team's copy, so every machine downloads from it over your own network into its own cache. You can also combine them.

docs.title: Option 1: a cache folder on shared storage
docs.text:
huggingface_hub reads the cache location from HF_HUB_CACHE, or from HF_HOME with hub added. Point every machine at a folder on a network file system, such as NFS or SMB:

export HF_HUB_CACHE=/mnt/models/hub

The first machine to load a model downloads it into the folder, and the others find it there. This needs nothing new to run, but the cache was designed as a local folder. Check these points first:

  • Every machine that downloads needs write access to the whole folder. huggingface_hub takes file locks in the cache while it downloads, so two machines that ask for the same file at once wait for each other only if the file system supports those locks.
  • Snapshots link to files in blobs/. On a file system that does not handle symbolic links well, set HF_HUB_DISABLE_SYMLINKS=1 on every machine, so files are copied into snapshots/ instead. A file can then be stored once per Revision.
  • Anyone who can read the folder can read every model in it, including models from private or gated Repos that someone else downloaded with their own token.
  • Only machines that mount the share can use it. CI runners, laptops away from the office and Kubernetes nodes each need the mount.
  • Each new model or Revision is still downloaded from huggingface.co, with whatever token the person who asked for it had.

To share a cache that machines only read, fill it from one machine, mount it read-only on the others, and set HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 there, so the libraries load from the cache without making any requests.

docs.title: Option 2: Hangar as the team's copy
docs.text:
Hangar keeps one copy of each model on the Instance and serves it with the Hugging Face Hub API. Each machine keeps its own local cache as usual, and HF_ENDPOINT sends its downloads to Hangar instead of huggingface.co:

export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hangar.example.com
export HF_TOKEN=hgr_...

Code does not change, and a Revision pinned to a Commit SHA works as it does on huggingface.co, because each Mirror keeps the upstream Repo ID and Commit SHAs. Compared with a shared folder:

  • Downloads go over your own network, and huggingface.co sees one download per file, from Hangar's Pull.
  • Each person signs in with their own Token, and Organisations and Roles decide who can read which Repos, including private and gated ones.
  • Anything that can reach the Instance over HTTPS can use it: laptops, CI runners and Kubernetes Pods, with no file system mount.
  • The Instance also holds models and datasets you upload, and serves GGUF models to Ollama and LM Studio.

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text:
1. Run an Instance where the team can reach it.

  2. If you already have a large cache, such as a shared folder from option 1, import it, so Hangar does not download those files again:

    hangar import --from-hf-cache /mnt/models/hub

    Each cached Repo becomes a Mirror of the huggingface.co Repo at the cached Commit. See Importing an existing cache.

  3. Pull the other models the team uses. --server-only fills the Arsenal without downloading to your machine:

    hangar pull Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --server-only

    To keep a model up to date, add --track. To let a request for a model that is not in the Arsenal start its Pull, an admin can turn on Pull-through.

  4. For gated models, save a huggingface.co token under Settings, Upstream tokens, or set an Instance token for the Upstream. See Gated models.

  5. Each person creates a Token under Settings, Tokens, then sets HF_ENDPOINT and HF_TOKEN. After hangar login, eval "$(hangar env)" sets both. See Point HF_ENDPOINT at Hangar.

docs.title: Combine the two
docs.text:
On a cluster of GPU machines that share a file system, you can use both: Hangar as the source, and a shared cache folder that the machines only read.

Fill the shared folder from Hangar on one machine. hangar pull writes into a Hugging Face cache in the same layout the Python libraries read:

hangar pull Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --cache-dir /mnt/models/hub

Then load from the folder on every machine with no network requests:

export HF_HUB_CACHE=/mnt/models/hub
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
python train.py

Only the machine that fills the folder needs write access and a Token. hangar pull creates the cache folders readable by its own user and group only, so run it as a user in a group that the readers share.

docs.title: Which to choose
docs.text: Shared cache folder Hangar Something new to run No One Instance Who can read what Anyone who can read the folder Per User, Organisation and Repo Works without a file system mount No Yes, over HTTPS Downloads from huggingface.co Once per new file, by whoever asks first Once per file, by the Instance Your own models and datasets No Yes, with uploads and git Ollama and LM Studio No Yes

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Python libraries and the hf CLI: use Hangar from Python and the shell.
  • Hugging Face rate limits in CI: stop CI jobs downloading models from huggingface.co.
  • Kubernetes model loading: keep models on a volume across Pod restarts.
  • Where Hangar keeps data: where the Instance and the CLI keep files.

docs.title: Upload models and datasets
docs.text:
You can upload in five ways. All of them create real Commits, and a large file that already exists anywhere in the Instance is not stored twice.

Way Use it for huggingface_hub (upload_file, upload_folder, create_commit) Code that already uploads to the Hub. The hf CLI (hf upload) One-off uploads from a shell. hangar push Folders of any size, with resumable multipart uploads. git push with git-lfs Repos you already manage with git. See git and git-lfs. The web UI Drag and drop files or folders. Uploads go straight to the Blob store in parallel parts and resume after a dropped connection.

docs.title: With huggingface_hub
docs.text:
from huggingface_hub import HfApi

api = HfApi()  # HF_ENDPOINT and HF_TOKEN point at Hangar
api.create_repo("acme/my-model", private=True, exist_ok=True)
api.upload_folder(repo_id="acme/my-model", folder_path="./weights", commit_message="First weights")
api.upload_file(path_or_fileobj="README.md", path_in_repo="README.md", repo_id="acme/my-model", create_pr=True)

docs.title: With and without hf_xet
docs.text:
huggingface_hub installs hf_xet by default on x86_64 and arm64, and then uploads every large file through the Xet protocol. Hangar accepts Xet uploads and stores whole files, so this works with no setup. Downloads always use plain HTTP.

If you turned Xet uploads off on the Instance (hfapi.xet: reject), set HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1 on clients, so they use classic LFS uploads instead.

Files over lfs.multipart_threshold (64 MiB by default) go up in parts, and a single file can be up to 5 TiB.

Small files that are not stored with LFS (under hfapi.regular_upload_max, 10 MiB by default) travel inside the commit request itself. One commit can carry up to hfapi.commit_inline_max of them (1 GiB by default) and gets HTTP 413 above that. To upload a larger folder of small files, such as a dataset of many JSON Lines files, use upload_large_folder, which splits the upload into several commits.

docs.title: With hangar push
docs.text:
hangar push ./my-finetune acme/my-finetune --create --private -m "First upload"
hangar push ./data datasets/acme/reviews --branch march

hangar push hashes every file, asks the Instance which ones it needs, uploads only those, in parts, then makes one Commit. If an upload stops part-way, run the same command again: parts already stored are not sent again. A file that still fails after its retries does not stop the others: the command uploads the rest, names the files that failed and makes no Commit, so the next run sends only those files and then commits. .git and huggingface_hub's .cache/huggingface folder are skipped; add --include and --exclude patterns for more control, or --create-pr to open a pull request instead.

After the last part of a large file, the Instance checks its SHA-256 and size and stores it, which takes about 20 seconds per GiB on a small host. While it does, the CLI shows Verifying <file> (<size>) on the Instance with the time taken. It waits up to 5 minutes for the answer, or 40 seconds per GiB for a file larger than 7.5 GiB.
