docs.title: Report a vulnerability
docs.text:
Please report security problems privately, through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting: open the repository's Security tab and select Report a vulnerability. Do not open a public issue, discussion or pull request for a vulnerability.

Include what you found, how to reproduce it, the version or commit, and the impact you expect. You should get an answer within a week. Once a fix is ready, we publish a GitHub security advisory and a release, and credit you if you want to be credited.

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text: Security fixes go into the latest minor release. Upgrade to it to get them; see Upgrades.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: In scope: the hangar binary and container image, the Helm chart and the Compose examples in this repository. Out of scope: vulnerabilities in models or datasets that users store in Hangar (for example malicious pickle files, which Hangar scans and flags but does not run), and denial of service through traffic volume, which a reverse proxy in front of Hangar should limit.

docs.title: Hardening
docs.text: See Security hardening, which also explains how to verify image signatures.

docs.title: Get help
docs.text: Hangar is maintained by one person, in the open on GitHub. There is no paid support, no chat channel and no guaranteed response time, so the steps below are the quickest way to an answer.

docs.title: Before you ask
docs.text:
1. Run hangar admin doctor on the server host. It checks the configuration, the database, the Blob store and git, and says which check fails; see Troubleshooting.
  2. Read Troubleshooting and the FAQ.
  3. Search the existing issues, open and closed, for the error message.

docs.title: Open an issue
docs.text:
Questions, problems and ideas all go to GitHub issues. Choose the form that fits:

Form Use it for Bug report Something does not work as documented. This includes documentation that is wrong, or that leaves you unable to finish a task. Compatibility gap A client that works with huggingface.co, git, Ollama or LM Studio does not work with Hangar. Feature request Something Hangar should do but does not.

Include:

  • The output of hangar version, and how you run Hangar: Docker, Docker Compose, Helm or the binary.
  • The database and Blob store, such as SQLite and the filesystem, or Postgres and MinIO.
  • The commands or code that show the problem, and what you expected.
  • The output of hangar admin doctor, and the log lines around the error. A server error names its request ID; search the logs for that request_id to find the cause.

Remove secrets first: Tokens (hgr_...), passwords, the Instance key, Authorization headers, cookies and presigned URLs.

docs.title: Security problems
docs.text: Do not open a public issue for a vulnerability. Report it privately, as the security policy describes.

docs.title: Licence questions
docs.text: What you can and cannot do with Hangar is on the Licence page and in the FAQ.

docs.title: Version numbers
docs.text:
Hangar follows semantic versioning: versions are MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, such as 1.2.3. release-please proposes each version from the Conventional Commits merged since the last release, and writes the changelog:

Release Example What it can contain Patch 1.2.2 to 1.2.3 Bug fixes, dependency updates and documentation changes. 1.2.1 and 1.2.3 changed only the documentation. Minor 1.1.0 to 1.2.0 New features, as well as fixes. Major 1.x to 2.0.0 Changes that are not backward compatible. The changelog lists them under BREAKING CHANGES.

There has been no major release since 1.0.0.

Within a major version, database migrations only add to the schema, so processes of the previous version keep working while you upgrade. Migrations do not run backwards: to go back to an earlier version, restore a backup made with it.

The native API has its own version, in its path (/api/hangar/v1) and in its OpenAPI description (1.0.0). It is the version of the API, not of Hangar.

docs.title: Release schedule
docs.text: There is no fixed schedule. A release goes out when the release pull request that release-please keeps open is merged; the release workflow then publishes the binaries, the container image, the Helm chart, the Homebrew cask and the documentation. The releases page and the changelog list every release.

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text:
Security fixes go into the latest minor release, as the security policy says. Older minor releases do not get fixes, so to get a fix, upgrade to the latest release.

Hangar is maintained by one person. There is no paid support and no guaranteed response time; see Get help.

docs.title: How versions line up
docs.text:
Every artefact of a release carries the same version:

Artefact Names For release 1.2.3 Git tag and GitHub release vX.Y.Z v1.2.3 Container image ghcr.io/hangar-hub/hangar:X.Y.Z, :X.Y and :latest, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. There is no tag for a major version alone. :1.2.3, :1.2 Helm chart oci://ghcr.io/hangar-hub/charts/hangar, whose chart version and appVersion are both X.Y.Z --version 1.2.3 Release archives hangar_X.Y.Z_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz, or .zip for Windows hangar_1.2.3_linux_amd64.tar.gz Homebrew cask hangar-hub/tap/hangar 1.2.3 Documentation One version per minor release, at /X.Y/. /latest/ is the newest release and /dev/ follows the main branch. /1.2/, also /latest/

To follow patch releases of one minor version, use the :X.Y image tag. To change versions only when you choose to, pin :X.Y.Z. :latest moves to every new release, including minor releases.

docs.title: Find the version you run
docs.text:
• hangar version prints it, from a release archive, Homebrew or the image: docker exec hangar hangar version. Builds made with go install report dev.
  • In the web UI, Instance admins see it under Admin, System.
  • On Kubernetes, helm list --namespace <namespace> shows the chart and app version.

docs.title: Clients and platforms
docs.text: Which versions of huggingface_hub, git, Ollama, Postgres and Kubernetes each release is tested with, and on which platforms, is in Tested versions and platforms.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
• Hub API compatibility: every Hugging Face Hub endpoint and whether Hangar supports it, generated from the compatibility suite.
  • Tested versions and platforms: the client, database and platform versions CI tests against.
  • Native API: the API behind the web UI and the CLI, from its OpenAPI description.
  • CLI: every hangar command and flag, generated from the binary.
  • Configuration: every configuration key, generated from the binary.
  • Webhook events.
  • Metrics: every metric Hangar exports, generated from the binary.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
hangar is one binary for the server and the client. Client commands talk to an Instance through the Hub API and the native API; admin commands work on an Instance's database and Blob store directly.

Every client command takes --url, --token and --json. Without --url and --token, they use the login saved by hangar login, or the HANGAR_CLI_URL and HANGAR_CLI_TOKEN environment variables.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success. 1 An error. 2 A usage error, such as a missing argument or an unknown flag. 3 Not found, such as a Repo or a file. 4 An authentication error: not signed in, or the Token is not allowed.

docs.title: hangar admin
docs.text:
Administer an Instance directly through its database and Blob store.

Subcommands:

  • hangar admin backup: Back up the database and the Blob store to a folder
  • hangar admin create-user: Create a local user
  • hangar admin doctor: Check the configuration, database, Blob store, presigned URLs, clock and git
  • hangar admin gc: Collect garbage: unreferenced LFS objects and unused git data
  • hangar admin migrate: Apply database migrations
  • hangar admin reindex: Index and scan Repos again
  • hangar admin reset-password: Set a local user's password
  • hangar admin restore: Restore a backup made by hangar admin backup
  • hangar admin rotate-key: Replace the Instance key and re-encrypt every stored secret
  • hangar admin unlock-sign-in: Clear sign-in throttling for a user or an IP address

docs.title: hangar admin backup
docs.text:
Back up the database and the Blob store to a folder.

Writes a backup folder: manifest.json, every database table as JSON Lines in
db/, and every Blob store object in blobs/ under its key. Staging objects
(tmp/, uploads/ and exports/) are left out.

The database is read in one transaction, so it is consistent. Objects are
copied after it; LFS objects and git packs never change once written, and
garbage collection keeps unreferenced objects for gc.grace_period, so every
object the database references is in the backup.

With SQLite, stop Hangar first: only one process may open the database. With
Postgres, the backup can run while Hangar is running. With --skip-blobs, back
up the Blob store with the storage's own tools instead (for example bucket
replication or a filesystem snapshot).

Usage:

hangar admin backup [flags]

Examples:

hangar admin backup --output /backups/hangar-$(date +%F)
hangar admin backup --output /backups/db-only --skip-blobs

Flags:

Flag Description Default -c, --config YAML configuration file (or set HANGAR_CONFIG) --json print JSON instead of text -o, --output folder to write the backup to; must not exist or be empty --set set a configuration key, such as --set database.dsn=... (repeatable) --skip-blobs back up the database only

docs.title: hangar admin create-user
docs.text:
Create a local user.

Creates a local user with a personal Namespace. The password is read from
standard input with --password-stdin, or generated and printed once.

Usage:

hangar admin create-user <username> [flags]

Flags:

Flag Description Default --admin make the user an Instance admin -c, --config YAML configuration file (or set HANGAR_CONFIG) --display-name the user's display name --email the user's email address --json print JSON instead of text --listen shortcut for --set server.listen=... --password-stdin read the password from standard input instead of generating one --public-url shortcut for --set server.public_url=... --role shortcut for --set server.role=... --set set a configuration key, such as --set storage.backend=s3 (repeatable)

docs.title: hangar admin doctor
docs.text:
Check the configuration, database, Blob store, presigned URLs, clock and git.

Runs the same kind of checks as the readiness endpoint, with more detail:
the configuration, the database connection and schema version, the clock
against the database, a write, read and delete in the Blob store, presigned
downloads on S3, and the git version. Exits with 1 if any check fails.

With --large-read, it also writes an object of that size (1100 MiB if no
size is given) to the Blob store and reads it back in one request at
16 MiB/s, more slowly than the store sends, as Hangar does when it checks
a large upload on a small server. A proxy in front of the store that cuts
long reads, such as nginx with its default proxy_max_temp_file_size of
1024 MiB, fails this check. It takes over a minute at the default size
and deletes the object afterwards.

Usage:

hangar admin doctor [flags]

Examples:

hangar admin doctor --config /etc/hangar/hangar.yaml
hangar admin doctor --config /etc/hangar/hangar.yaml --large-read
hangar admin doctor --config /etc/hangar/hangar.yaml --large-read=3GiB

Flags:

Flag Description Default -c, --config YAML configuration file (or set HANGAR_CONFIG) --json print JSON instead of text --large-read also write an object of this size and read it back slowly in one request, to find a proxy that cuts long reads --set set a configuration key, such as --set database.dsn=... (repeatable)

docs.title: hangar admin gc
docs.text:
Collect garbage: unreferenced LFS objects and unused git data.

Deletes LFS objects no Repo has referenced for gc.grace_period, orphaned
LFS objects in the Blob store, retired and orphaned packs, git data of
purged Repos, stale temporary files and abandoned uploads, then reports
what it freed. It runs in this process; with --queue it queues a gc Job
for the Instance's workers instead, which needs a running Instance on
Postgres.

Usage:

hangar admin gc [flags]

Flags:

Flag Description Default -c, --config YAML configuration file (or set HANGAR_CONFIG) --git collect git data only --json print JSON instead of text --lfs collect LFS objects only --listen shortcut for --set server.listen=... --public-url shortcut for --set server.public_url=... --queue queue a gc Job for the Instance's workers instead of running it here --role shortcut for --set server.role=... --set set a configuration key, such as --set storage.backend=s3 (repeatable)

docs.title: hangar admin migrate
docs.text:
Apply database migrations.

Applies every pending migration. The Helm chart runs it in a pre-install and pre-upgrade Job, or in an init container of each web and worker Pod. Migrators that start together wait for one another. With --wait-for-database, it also waits for a Postgres server that does not answer yet, such as one whose Pod is still starting.

Usage:

hangar admin migrate [flags]

Flags:

Flag Description Default -c, --config YAML configuration file (or set HANGAR_CONFIG) --json print JSON instead of text --listen shortcut for --set server.listen=... --public-url shortcut for --set server.public_url=... --role shortcut for --set server.role=... --set set a configuration key, such as --set storage.backend=s3 (repeatable) --wait-for-database how long to keep trying to connect while a Postgres database does not answer (0 fails at once) 0s

docs.title: hangar admin reindex
docs.text:
Index and scan Repos again.

Queues index and scan Jobs for the head of every branch of the named Repos,
or of every Repo when none is named. With --stale it queues them only for
results from an older indexer or scanner version, as workers do when they
start. The Instance's workers run the Jobs; on SQLite they run when Hangar
starts again.

Name a Repo as namespace/name, or datasets/namespace/name for a dataset.

Usage:

hangar admin reindex [repo...] [flags]

Flags:

Flag Description Default -c, --config YAML configuration file (or set HANGAR_CONFIG) --json print JSON instead of text --listen shortcut for --set server.listen=... --public-url shortcut for --set server.public_url=... --role shortcut for --set server.role=... --set set a configuration key, such as --set storage.backend=s3 (repeatable) --stale queue Jobs only for results from an older indexer or scanner version --type the type of Repo IDs without a prefix: model (the default) or dataset

docs.title: hangar admin reset-password
docs.text:
Set a local user's password.

Sets a new password for a user, signs them out everywhere and clears
sign-in throttling, for example when the only admin is locked out. The
password is read from standard input with --password-stdin, or generated
and printed once. To let a user choose their own, create a reset link in
the admin UI instead.

Usage:

hangar admin reset-password <username> [flags]

Flags:

Flag Description Default -c, --config YAML configuration file (or set HANGAR_CONFIG) --json print JSON instead of text --listen shortcut for --set server.listen=... --password-stdin read the password from standard input instead of generating one --public-url shortcut for --set server.public_url=... --role shortcut for --set server.role=... --set set a configuration key, such as --set storage.backend=s3 (repeatable)

docs.title: hangar admin restore
docs.text:
Restore a backup made by hangar admin backup.

Restores a backup folder into the configured database and Blob store. The
database is migrated first, and must then be at the same schema version as
the backup: restore with the Hangar version that made the backup, then
upgrade. The database must be empty unless --force is given, which deletes
every row first.

Rows are written in one transaction, so a failed restore leaves the database
as it was. Objects already in the Blob store with the right size are not
copied again. A backup from SQLite restores into Postgres and the other way
round, and a filesystem backup restores into S3 and the other way round.

Stop every Hangar process first.

Usage:

hangar admin restore <backup-folder> [flags]

Examples:

hangar admin restore /backups/hangar-2026-10-13
hangar admin restore /backups/hangar-2026-10-13 --set database.driver=postgres --set database.dsn=postgres://...

Flags:

Flag Description Default -c, --config YAML configuration file (or set HANGAR_CONFIG) --force delete every row in the database before restoring --json print JSON instead of text --set set a configuration key, such as --set database.dsn=... (repeatable) --skip-blobs restore the database only

docs.title: hangar admin rotate-key
docs.text:
Replace the Instance key and re-encrypt every stored secret.

Generates a new security.instance_key (or uses --new-key) and, in one
database transaction, re-encrypts every secret sealed with the old key:
users' Upstream tokens, the Instance's token for each Upstream, and webhook
secrets.

Stop every Hangar process first: a process still running with the old key
cannot read the re-encrypted secrets. If the key came from secrets.yaml in
server.data_dir, the file is updated. Otherwise the new key is printed once;
put it in your configuration, environment or Kubernetes Secret before you
start Hangar again.

Usage:

hangar admin rotate-key [flags]

Flags:

Flag Description Default -c, --config YAML configuration file (or set HANGAR_CONFIG) --json print JSON instead of text --new-key the new key, 32 bytes base64-encoded (default: generate one) --set set a configuration key, such as --set database.dsn=... (repeatable)

docs.title: hangar admin unlock-sign-in
docs.text:
Clear sign-in throttling for a user or an IP address.

Clears the sign-in throttle for a username, an IP address (--ip), or every
username and address (--all), so they can sign in again at once. Use it when
failed sign-ins, perhaps someone else's, have locked out an account you need,
such as the bootstrap admin. The password is not changed; to change it, use
hangar admin reset-password instead.

Usage:

hangar admin unlock-sign-in [username] [flags]

Examples:

hangar admin unlock-sign-in hangar-admin
hangar admin unlock-sign-in --ip 192.0.2.10
hangar admin unlock-sign-in --all

Flags:

Flag Description Default --all clear the throttle of every username and IP address -c, --config YAML configuration file (or set HANGAR_CONFIG) --ip clear the throttle of this client IP address --json print JSON instead of text --listen shortcut for --set server.listen=... --public-url shortcut for --set server.public_url=... --role shortcut for --set server.role=... --set set a configuration key, such as --set storage.backend=s3 (repeatable)

docs.text:
Print environment variables that point Python tools at the Instance.

Prints HF_ENDPOINT and HF_TOKEN for the current Instance, so huggingface_hub,

It also prints DISABLE_SAFETENSORS_CONVERSION=1. Without it, transformers can
send the Repo ID of a model that has only pickle weights, and any Token passed
to it, to a conversion service on huggingface.co.

Usage:

Examples:

eval "$(hangar env)"
hangar env --shell fish | source

docs.title: hangar healthcheck
docs.text:
Call /readyz on this host and exit 0 when ready.

Calls /readyz on the local listen address. The container image uses it as its HEALTHCHECK.

With --retry-for, it tries again while the connection fails, for up to that long. A check
through a Kubernetes Service needs this: the Service starts routing to a new Pod a moment
after the Pod is ready, and until then it refuses connections. An answer from /readyz,
ready or not, is never retried.

Usage:

hangar healthcheck [flags]

Flags:

Flag Description Default -c, --config YAML configuration file (or set HANGAR_CONFIG) --json print JSON instead of text --listen shortcut for --set server.listen=... --public-url shortcut for --set server.public_url=... --retry-for keep trying for this long while the connection fails, such as 30s (0 tries once) 0s --role shortcut for --set server.role=... --set set a configuration key, such as --set storage.backend=s3 (repeatable)

docs.title: hangar import
docs.text:
Add models you already have on disk to the Arsenal without pulling them again.

Adds content that is already on this machine to the Arsenal. Choose one source:

  --from-hf-cache [path]   a Hugging Face cache (default ~/.cache/huggingface/hub).
                           Each Repo becomes a Mirror of the Upstream Repo with
                           the same ID: the Instance fetches its history, and
                           the CLI uploads the files of every cached snapshot
                           whose content matches a file the Mirror is missing.
                           With --offline, or when the Upstream does not have
                           the Repo, each becomes a local Repo with one Commit
                           of the snapshot of main, or else the newest.
  --from-dir <dir>         a folder, uploaded to --repo as one Commit, as
                           hangar push does.
  --from-lmstudio [path]   LM Studio's models folder (<publisher>/<repo>/<files>).
                           Folders that match an Upstream Repo of the same name
                           become Partial mirrors; the rest become local Repos.
  --from-ollama            Ollama's models. Each model and tag becomes a local
                           Repo in your Namespace (or --namespace) with its GGUF
                           file and its template, system and params files.

Uploads go through the Instance's API, so you need write access to the
Namespaces involved. A file that fails to upload does not stop the other
files or Repos: files that went up into a Mirror are added to it, and the
results name what failed, so running the command again sends only that.
Files whose content matches nothing in a Mirror are named after the results,
with the reason. Use --dry-run to see what would be imported.

To import some models and not the rest, give --only once for each, as it
appears in the source: a Repo ID such as bartowski/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GGUF
for a Hugging Face cache, a <publisher>/<repo> folder for LM Studio, or a
model and tag such as llama3.2:1b for Ollama (llama3.2 means llama3.2:latest).
Patterns can use * and ?, which do not match /, and ignore case. A pattern
that matches nothing stops the import before anything is uploaded.

Usage:

hangar import [flags]

Examples:

hangar import --from-hf-cache
hangar import --from-hf-cache /mnt/models/hf --offline --namespace acme
hangar import --from-hf-cache --only 'bartowski/*' --only Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct --dry-run
hangar import --from-dir ./weights --repo acme/my-model
hangar import --from-lmstudio
hangar import --from-ollama --namespace acme

Flags:

Flag Description Default --dry-run only list what would be imported --from-dir import a folder as one Commit to --repo --from-hf-cache import a Hugging Face cache --from-lmstudio import LM Studio's models folder --from-ollama import Ollama's models --json print JSON instead of text --namespace Namespace for local Repos (default: the Repo's own, or yours for Ollama models) --offline never ask the Upstream; create local Repos --ollama-models Ollama's models folder (default: $OLLAMA_MODELS or ~/.ollama/models) --only only import models matching this pattern, such as 'bartowski/*' or llama3.2:1b (repeatable) --private make new local Repos private --repo with --from-dir, the Repo to import into, such as acme/model or datasets/acme/data --token Token to use instead of the saved login (or HANGAR_CLI_TOKEN) --upstream Upstream that Mirrors track huggingface --url Instance URL (default: from hangar login, or HANGAR_CLI_URL)

docs.title: hangar info

docs.title: hangar lmstudio
docs.text:
Install Hangar models into LM Studio.

Installs models from the Instance into LM Studio's models folder, laid out as
<namespace>/<name>/<files>. Files are downloaded once into the local Hugging
Face cache and linked into LM Studio's folder, so the disk is used once even
when Python libraries use the same model.

The models folder is --lmstudio-dir if given; otherwise the downloadsFolder in
LM Studio's settings.json, in LM Studio's home folder (the path in
~/.lmstudio-home-pointer, else ~/.cache/lm-studio, else ~/.lmstudio);
otherwise the models folder in that home folder.

Subcommands:

  • hangar lmstudio install: Download a model and link it into LM Studio
  • hangar lmstudio list: List models installed from Hangar, and whether a newer Revision exists
  • hangar lmstudio remove: Remove a model's links from LM Studio

docs.text:

hangar lmstudio install bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M

docs.title: hangar login
docs.text:
Sign in to an Instance and save the Token.

Signs in to an Instance. Without --token, starts a device-code login: the
browser opens a page on the Instance where you type the code shown here,
check the details and approve it. The Instance then creates a Token for the
CLI that expires in 30 days, with read access, or write access if you choose
it on that page (needed to push, upload and pull into the Instance).

The URL and username are saved in ~/.config/hangar/config.yaml. The Token is
saved in the OS keychain where one is available, otherwise in that file with
mode 0600. Pass --token - to read the Token from standard input.

Usage:

hangar login [flags]

Examples:

hangar login --url https://hangar.example.com
hangar login --url http://localhost:8080 --token hgr_xxxxxxxx
echo "$TOKEN" | hangar login --url https://hangar.example.com --token -

Flags:

Flag Description Default --json print JSON instead of text --no-browser print the approval link instead of opening a browser --token Token to use instead of the saved login (or HANGAR_CLI_TOKEN) --url Instance URL (default: from hangar login, or HANGAR_CLI_URL)

docs.title: hangar logout
docs.text:

The Token itself stays valid until you revoke it in the web UI under
Settings, Tokens.

Usage:

hangar logout [flags]

Flags:

Flag Description Default --json print JSON instead of text

docs.title: hangar ollama
docs.text:
Install Hangar GGUF models into Ollama.

Subcommands:

  • hangar ollama install: Pull a GGUF model into Ollama from the Instance
  • hangar ollama key: Manage your Ollama key on the Instance

Flags:

Flag Description Default --json print JSON instead of text --token Token to use instead of the saved login (or HANGAR_CLI_TOKEN) --url Instance URL (default: from hangar login, or HANGAR_CLI_URL)

docs.title: hangar ollama install
docs.text:
Pull a GGUF model into Ollama from the Instance.

Runs ollama pull <host>/<namespace>/<name>:<quant> against the Instance, adding
--insecure for an http:// Instance.

Before that, checks that the quant is in the Arsenal. Without a quant, Ollama
asks for "latest", which is Q4_K_M or the closest quant. Ollama shows only
"file does not exist" for a quant the Instance has not pulled, so when it is
missing this command says so, prints the hangar pull command that pulls it
into the Instance, and offers to run it (--pull runs it without asking).

Then checks that your Ollama key (~/.ollama/id_ed25519.pub) is registered with
the Instance, and offers to register it. Ollama needs the key for every Repo
unless the Repo is public and the Instance allows anonymous reads
(security.anonymous_read, off by default).

Usage:

hangar ollama install <repo>[:<quant>] [flags]

Examples:

hangar ollama install bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M
hangar ollama install bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q8_0 --pull
hangar ollama install acme/private-model --yes

Flags:

Flag Description Default --pull pull the quant into the Instance first, without asking, if it is not in the Arsenal --skip-key-check do not check the Ollama key, for public Repos on an Instance that allows anonymous reads -y, --yes register the Ollama key without asking

Inherited flags:

Flag Description Default --json print JSON instead of text --token Token to use instead of the saved login (or HANGAR_CLI_TOKEN) --url Instance URL (default: from hangar login, or HANGAR_CLI_URL)

Registers your Ollama key (~/.ollama/id_ed25519.pub) with the Instance, unless

docs.title: hangar pull
docs.text:
Pull a Repo into the Arsenal and download it to the local cache.

Makes sure the Repo, or the files you choose, are in the Arsenal: if they are
not, asks the Instance to pull them from an Upstream and shows the progress.
Then downloads them into the local Hugging Face cache, where Python libraries
pointed at the same Instance find them, or into a folder with --to.

Choose files with a GGUF quant after a colon, --include and --exclude
patterns, or, for datasets, --config, --split and --parquet-only. With
--server-only, nothing is downloaded to this machine.

Usage:

hangar pull <repo>[:<quant>] [flags]

Examples:

hangar pull bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M
hangar pull hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-bert --include '*.json' --include '*.safetensors'
hangar pull datasets/lhoestq/demo1 --config default --split train --parquet-only --to ./data
hangar pull Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --server-only

Flags:

Flag Description Default --cache-dir Hugging Face cache folder (default: $HF_HUB_CACHE or ~/.cache/huggingface/hub) --config dataset Config to pull (repeatable) --exclude skip files matching this pattern (repeatable) --include only files matching this pattern, such as '*.safetensors' (repeatable) --json print JSON instead of text --now start the Pull now, outside the Instance's pull windows, if allowed --parquet-only pull and download only the dataset's Parquet export --revision branch, tag or Commit SHA (default: the default branch) --server-only only pull into the Arsenal; download nothing --split dataset Split to pull (repeatable) --to download into this folder instead of the Hugging Face cache --token Token to use instead of the saved login (or HANGAR_CLI_TOKEN) --track make a new Mirror follow its upstream branch --type Repo type for IDs without a prefix: model or dataset --upstream Upstream to pull from when the Repo is not in the Arsenal huggingface --url Instance URL (default: from hangar login, or HANGAR_CLI_URL)

docs.title: hangar push
docs.text:
Upload a folder to a Repo as one Commit.

Uploads every file under a folder as one Commit. Large files go up in parts,
straight to the Blob store where the Instance allows it, and an interrupted
upload resumes from the parts already stored when you run the command again.
A part that fails for a reason that may pass, such as a dropped connection
or a 503 from a proxy, is sent again up to 6 times with a growing wait, and
part URLs that expired are renewed. When finishing an upload fails for a
reason that may pass (the Instance answers 503 with Retry-After, a proxy
cuts the request off, or no answer comes within 5 minutes, or 40 seconds
per GiB for a file larger than 7.5 GiB), the command waits and tries again,
up to 10 times.

A file that still fails does not stop the others: the command uploads the
rest, names the files that failed and makes no Commit, so running it again
sends only those files.
Files the Instance already has anywhere are not sent again.

With --branch, a branch that does not exist yet is created from the default
branch before the upload starts.

The .git folder and huggingface_hub's .cache/huggingface folder are skipped.

Usage:

hangar push <dir> <repo> [flags]

Examples:

hangar push ./my-finetune acme/my-finetune --create --private
hangar push ./data datasets/acme/reviews --message "Add the March export"
hangar push ./out acme/model --branch experiment --include '*.safetensors'

Flags:

Flag Description Default --branch branch to commit to, created from the default branch if it does not exist (default: the default branch) --create create the Repo if it does not exist --create-pr open a pull request instead of committing to the branch --description longer Commit description --exclude skip files matching this pattern (repeatable) --include only upload files matching this pattern (repeatable) --json print JSON instead of text -m, --message Commit message Upload with hangar push --private with --create, make the new Repo private --token Token to use instead of the saved login (or HANGAR_CLI_TOKEN) --type Repo type for IDs without a prefix: model or dataset --url Instance URL (default: from hangar login, or HANGAR_CLI_URL)

docs.title: hangar search
docs.text:
Search the Arsenal, or an Upstream with --upstream.

Searches the Repos you can see in the Arsenal. With --upstream, searches an
Upstream instead (Discover) and marks each result as in the Arsenal, partly in
the Arsenal, or not.

Filters for the Arsenal are key=value pairs: format, task, library, quant,
licence, ns, params_min, params_max, context_min, size_max, mirror, modality,
language and size_category. Filters for an Upstream are its tags, such as
gguf, mlx or text-generation.

Usage:

hangar search [query] [flags]

Examples:

hangar search llama --filter format=gguf --filter quant=Q4_K_M
hangar search --type dataset --filter task=text-classification
hangar search qwen --upstream --filter gguf --sort downloads

Flags:

Flag Description Default --filter filter results (repeatable); see above --json print JSON instead of text --limit maximum number of results, up to 500 50 --sort sort order. For the Arsenal: updated, name, size, parameters, downloads or likes. For an Upstream: trending, downloads, likes or lastModified --token Token to use instead of the saved login (or HANGAR_CLI_TOKEN) --type Repo type: model or dataset model --upstream search this Upstream instead of the Arsenal (default: huggingface) --url Instance URL (default: from hangar login, or HANGAR_CLI_URL)

docs.title: Tested versions and platforms
docs.text:
Hangar's CI runs the client compatibility suites in compat/ on every pull request and every night, against a real hangar binary as well as the Go test server (compat.yml). This page lists the versions they use, as of Hangar 1.2.3.

For each Hugging Face Hub endpoint and whether Hangar serves it, see Hub API compatibility.

docs.title: Hugging Face clients
docs.text:
Client Tested Runs huggingface_hub and the hf CLI 2.2.0, the latest, and 1.31.0, the oldest Every pull request and nightly Python 3.10 (with huggingface_hub 1.31.0), 3.11 (the default) and 3.14 Every pull request and nightly hf_xet 1.7.0 with the whole suite; 1.6.0 and 1.7.0 in the Xet upload suite; and the whole suite again without hf_xet installed Every pull request and nightly transformers 5.19.0 Every pull request and nightly sentence-transformers 5.7.0 Every pull request and nightly datasets 5.1.0 Every pull request and nightly torch 2.14.1 Every pull request and nightly diffusers 0.41.0, with huggingface_hub 1.33.0 Nightly only

1.31.0 is the oldest huggingface_hub that transformers 5.19.0 and datasets 5.1.0 accept. Older versions may work, but nothing tests them.

The suite runs against both databases, SQLite and Postgres, and with Xet uploads both on and off. Uploads of 200 MB files run on every pull request, and of a 6 GiB file nightly.

docs.title: git, Ollama and LM Studio
docs.text: Client Tested Notes git and git-lfs git 2.39 and git-lfs from Debian 12, and the versions on GitHub's Ubuntu 24.04 runners git 2.39 is also the oldest version the server needs. Ollama 0.31.1, the ollama/ollama image Hangar's Ollama registry follows this release's client behaviour. LM Studio The folder layout that hangar lmstudio install writes LM Studio is a desktop app, so loading a model in it is a manual check that compat/lmstudio describes.

docs.title: Databases, storage and deployment
docs.text: Component Tested Notes SQLite Built into Hangar One process in role all. Postgres 18 The Go tests and the Hub client suite run on Postgres as well as SQLite. S3-compatible storage MinIO in CI AWS S3 (eu-west-2) passed the suite on 15 October 2026. Other providers on the storage page are configured as described there, but are not in CI. Docker Compose The four examples in deploy/compose Each starts and passes the smoke test. Kubernetes The Helm chart needs Kubernetes 1.29 or later CI installs the chart on a kind cluster with Helm 4.1.3, runs helm test, a GitOps-style install with Postgres and MinIO, and the smoke test. Kibana 9.4 or later for the dashboard See Observability.

docs.text:
Platform Built Tested in CI Linux, amd64 and arm64 Binaries and the container image Go tests, a build and a server smoke test on both architectures. The container image runs in the Compose and Helm jobs on amd64. macOS, amd64 and arm64 Binaries and the Homebrew cask No Windows, amd64 and arm64 Binaries No

docs.text:
These guides describe tools that work through parts Hangar does test, such as huggingface_hub downloads and HfFileSystem, but CI does not run the tools themselves:

  • vLLM.
  • pandas and Polars over hf://, and DuckDB over HTTPS (Datasets).

docs.title: Report a gap
docs.text: If a client that works with huggingface.co fails with Hangar, open a compatibility gap issue with the client's version, the call that fails and its error, and whether the same call works against huggingface.co.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text:
Hangar reads its configuration from a YAML file (hangar server --config hangar.yaml, or the HANGAR_CONFIG environment variable), then from HANGAR_* environment variables, then from --set key=value flags. Later sources win. Hangar checks the whole configuration on start and reports every problem at once.

Every key is also an environment variable: storage.s3.bucket is HANGAR_STORAGE_S3_BUCKET. List values in environment variables and flags are comma-separated. oidc.providers takes a JSON array.

Sizes accept a number of bytes or a unit such as KiB, MiB, GiB or GB. Durations use Go syntax, such as 90s, 30m or 720h.

docs.title: server
docs.text:
HTTP server and process settings.

Key Type Default Description server.public_urlHANGAR_SERVER_PUBLIC_URL string "" The URL clients use to reach Hangar. Required. Used in redirects, LFS links and git URLs. server.listenHANGAR_SERVER_LISTEN string :8080 Address to listen on for HTTP. server.roleHANGAR_SERVER_ROLE string all Process role: all, web or worker. SQLite needs all. server.data_dirHANGAR_SERVER_DATA_DIR string /var/lib/hangar Directory for local state: the SQLite lock file and the generated secrets.yaml. server.trusted_proxiesHANGAR_SERVER_TRUSTED_PROXIES list of strings [] CIDR ranges of reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto headers Hangar trusts. server.max_request_bodyHANGAR_SERVER_MAX_REQUEST_BODY size 64MiB Body size limit for endpoints that buffer the request body. Streaming endpoints have no limit apart from quotas. server.shutdown_timeoutHANGAR_SERVER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT duration 30s How long to let in-flight requests finish on SIGTERM. Longer downloads are cut. server.drain_delayHANGAR_SERVER_DRAIN_DELAY duration 0s How long to keep serving after SIGTERM while /readyz answers 503, so load balancers stop sending requests before the listener closes. 0 closes at once; the Helm chart uses a preStop hook instead. server.timezoneHANGAR_SERVER_TIMEZONE string UTC IANA time zone for pull windows and schedules.

docs.title: database
docs.text:
Database connection.

Key Type Default Description database.driverHANGAR_DATABASE_DRIVER string sqlite sqlite or postgres. database.dsnHANGAR_DATABASE_DSN string /var/lib/hangar/hangar.db SQLite file path, or a postgres:// connection URL. database.max_open_connsHANGAR_DATABASE_MAX_OPEN_CONNS int 20 Maximum open database connections per process.

docs.title: storage
docs.text:
Blob store for LFS objects, git data and uploads.

Key Type Default Description storage.backendHANGAR_STORAGE_BACKEND string fs fs or s3. storage.fs.pathHANGAR_STORAGE_FS_PATH string /var/lib/hangar/blobs Root directory of the Blob store. storage.s3.endpointHANGAR_STORAGE_S3_ENDPOINT string s3.amazonaws.com S3 endpoint host, with an optional port. Use https:// or http:// to choose the scheme; the default is HTTPS. storage.s3.regionHANGAR_STORAGE_S3_REGION string eu-west-2 Bucket region. storage.s3.bucketHANGAR_STORAGE_S3_BUCKET string hangar Bucket name. storage.s3.prefixHANGAR_STORAGE_S3_PREFIX string "" Key prefix inside the bucket. storage.s3.access_key_idHANGAR_STORAGE_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID string "" Access key ID. Leave empty to use the default credential chain, IRSA or Workload Identity. storage.s3.secret_access_keyHANGAR_STORAGE_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY string "" Secret access key. storage.s3.use_path_styleHANGAR_STORAGE_S3_USE_PATH_STYLE bool false Use path-style bucket addressing, as MinIO and some other stores need. storage.s3.download_modeHANGAR_STORAGE_S3_DOWNLOAD_MODE string redirect redirect sends clients to presigned URLs; proxy streams bytes through Hangar. storage.s3.upload_modeHANGAR_STORAGE_S3_UPLOAD_MODE string direct direct gives clients presigned URLs to upload LFS objects and parts to the store; proxy has them upload through Hangar. Use proxy when clients cannot reach the endpoint. storage.s3.presign_ttlHANGAR_STORAGE_S3_PRESIGN_TTL duration 1h Lifetime of presigned download URLs. storage.s3.retriesHANGAR_STORAGE_S3_RETRIES int 5 How many times Hangar sends a failed part or object upload again, waiting longer each time. Part bodies are spooled to the temporary directory while they are sent. 0 turns retries off. storage.s3.startup_waitHANGAR_STORAGE_S3_STARTUP_WAIT duration 5m How long a server or worker keeps trying to reach the bucket at start, such as an object store whose Pod is still starting, before it exits. /readyz answers 503 while it waits. 0 exits at once. storage.s3.stall_timeoutHANGAR_STORAGE_S3_STALL_TIMEOUT duration 2m How long a request to the store may go without sending data or getting a response before Hangar cancels it and, for uploads, retries. Raise it on slow or congested links.

docs.title: security
docs.text:
Secrets, sign-in and access defaults.

Key Type Default Description security.instance_keyHANGAR_SECURITY_INSTANCE_KEY string "" 32-byte key, base64-encoded, that encrypts stored secrets and signs URLs. In role all, Hangar generates one in server.data_dir on first start if it is empty; roles web and worker never generate one, so set the same key on every process, or share one server.data_dir that already holds it. security.anonymous_readHANGAR_SECURITY_ANONYMOUS_READ bool false Let anonymous users read public Repos and see user and Organisation profiles. security.registrationHANGAR_SECURITY_REGISTRATION string closed Who can create an account: open, invite or closed. security.local_loginHANGAR_SECURITY_LOCAL_LOGIN bool true Show the username and password form. The bootstrap admin can always sign in at /auth/login?local=1. security.session_ttlHANGAR_SECURITY_SESSION_TTL duration 720h Lifetime of a UI session. security.session_idle_timeoutHANGAR_SECURITY_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT duration 168h A UI session not used for this long ends before session_ttl. 0 turns the idle timeout off. security.bootstrap_admin.usernameHANGAR_SECURITY_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME string hangar-admin Username of the bootstrap admin. security.bootstrap_admin.passwordHANGAR_SECURITY_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD string "" Password of the bootstrap admin. Generated on first start if empty and no password_file is set. security.bootstrap_admin.password_fileHANGAR_SECURITY_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE string "" File that holds the bootstrap admin password. security.bootstrap_admin.emailHANGAR_SECURITY_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL string "" Email address of the bootstrap admin.

docs.title: oidc
docs.text:
OpenID Connect sign-in providers.

Key Type Default Description oidc.providersHANGAR_OIDC_PROVIDERS list of objects [] Providers, shown as sign-in buttons. Set them in the YAML file, or as a JSON array in HANGAR_OIDC_PROVIDERS. oidc.providers[].id string Stable provider ID, used in callback URLs. oidc.providers[].name string Name on the sign-in button. oidc.providers[].issuer string Issuer URL, used for discovery. oidc.providers[].client_id string OAuth client ID. oidc.providers[].client_secret string (secret) OAuth client secret. Leave empty for public clients. oidc.providers[].scopes list of strings Scopes to request. oidc.providers[].claims map of strings Claim names for username, email, name and groups. oidc.providers[].admin_groups list of strings Members of these groups are Instance admins. Checked at every sign-in. oidc.providers[].org_mappings list of objects Groups that grant Organisation Roles. Checked at every sign-in. oidc.providers[].org_mappings[].group string Group claim value. oidc.providers[].org_mappings[].org string Organisation name. oidc.providers[].org_mappings[].role string read, write or admin. oidc.providers[].auto_create_users bool Create a User on first sign-in.

docs.title: upstreams
docs.text:
Upstreams that Hangar can Pull from, keyed by ID. huggingface is built in.

Key Type Default Description upstreams.<id>.base_urlHANGAR_UPSTREAMS_<ID>_BASE_URL string https://huggingface.co Base URL of the Upstream's Hub API. upstreams.<id>.enabledHANGAR_UPSTREAMS_<ID>_ENABLED bool true Whether users can Discover and Pull from this Upstream. upstreams.<id>.tokenHANGAR_UPSTREAMS_<ID>_TOKEN string "" Optional Instance token, used when the requesting user has not saved their own. upstreams.<id>.namespace_prefixHANGAR_UPSTREAMS_<ID>_NAMESPACE_PREFIX string "" Prefix for Mirror Namespaces from this Upstream, for example hf-. Prefixed Mirrors no longer work as drop-in HF_ENDPOINT replacements. upstreams.<id>.viewer_urlHANGAR_UPSTREAMS_<ID>_VIEWER_URL string "" Dataset Viewer URL of the Upstream. Default: the base URL with datasets-server. added to the host.

docs.title: pull
docs.text:
Pull scheduling and network controls.

Key Type Default Description pull.bandwidth_limitHANGAR_PULL_BANDWIDTH_LIMIT size 0 Bytes per second across the Instance. 0 means unlimited. pull.concurrencyHANGAR_PULL_CONCURRENCY int 4 Files transferred at once across the Instance. pull.windowsHANGAR_PULL_WINDOWS list of strings [] Times when Pull transfers may run, such as 01:00-07:00, in server.timezone. Empty means any time. pull.stall_timeoutHANGAR_PULL_STALL_TIMEOUT duration 2m How long an Upstream may take to answer a request, or go without sending data during a download, before Hangar cuts the connection and retries. Raise it on slow or congested links. pull.pull_through.enabledHANGAR_PULL_PULL_THROUGH_ENABLED bool false Turn on Pull-through. pull.pull_through.allowHANGAR_PULL_PULL_THROUGH_ALLOW list of strings [*] Globs of upstream Repo IDs that may be pulled through. pull.pull_through.min_roleHANGAR_PULL_PULL_THROUGH_MIN_ROLE string user Who may trigger Pull-through: anonymous or user (any signed-in user). pull.dependencies.auto_pull_codeHANGAR_PULL_DEPENDENCIES_AUTO_PULL_CODE bool true Pull code Dependencies (from auto_map) automatically. pull.dependencies.auto_pull_base_modelsHANGAR_PULL_DEPENDENCIES_AUTO_PULL_BASE_MODELS bool false Pull the base model of adapters automatically. pull.dependencies.max_depthHANGAR_PULL_DEPENDENCIES_MAX_DEPTH int 5 Maximum depth of recursive Dependency Pulls.

docs.title: git
docs.text:
git storage, push limits and the local pack cache.

Key Type Default Description git.max_blob_sizeHANGAR_GIT_MAX_BLOB_SIZE size 10MiB Largest non-LFS file accepted on push. git.max_pack_sizeHANGAR_GIT_MAX_PACK_SIZE size 2GiB Largest pack accepted on push. git.allow_force_pushHANGAR_GIT_ALLOW_FORCE_PUSH bool false Allow force-pushing default branches. Namespace admins always can. git.compact_thresholdHANGAR_GIT_COMPACT_THRESHOLD int 20 Compact a Repo's packs when it has more live packs than this. git.pack_grace_periodHANGAR_GIT_PACK_GRACE_PERIOD duration 1h How long retired packs are kept before deletion. Must be longer than the longest request. git.cache_dirHANGAR_GIT_CACHE_DIR string /var/cache/hangar/git Local pack cache directory. Disposable. git.cache_sizeHANGAR_GIT_CACHE_SIZE size 10GiB Size limit of the local pack cache. git.timeoutHANGAR_GIT_TIMEOUT duration 1h Wall-clock limit for one git operation.

docs.title: lfs
docs.text:
git-lfs uploads.

Key Type Default Description lfs.multipart_thresholdHANGAR_LFS_MULTIPART_THRESHOLD size 64MiB Objects larger than this use multipart uploads when the client supports them. lfs.upload_url_ttlHANGAR_LFS_UPLOAD_URL_TTL duration 24h Lifetime of signed upload URLs. lfs.verify_waitHANGAR_LFS_VERIFY_WAIT duration 10m How long a Commit waits for an LFS object that is still being verified.

docs.title: hfapi
docs.text:
Hugging Face Hub API behaviour.

Key Type Default Description hfapi.regular_upload_maxHANGAR_HFAPI_REGULAR_UPLOAD_MAX size 10MiB Preupload answers regular for files below this size unless .gitattributes says LFS. hfapi.commit_inline_maxHANGAR_HFAPI_COMMIT_INLINE_MAX size 1GiB Most bytes of regular (non-LFS) file content one Hub API commit may carry. Content past 32 MiB is spooled to the temporary directory, so this bounds the disk a commit can fill. Larger commits get 413. hfapi.xetHANGAR_HFAPI_XET string ingest ingest accepts Xet uploads; reject turns them off and asks clients to set HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1. hfapi.default_namespaceHANGAR_HFAPI_DEFAULT_NAMESPACE string "" Namespace that single-segment Repo IDs such as gpt2 redirect to. Empty turns the redirect off.

docs.title: xet
docs.text:
Xet upload ingestion.

Key Type Default Description xet.cas_urlHANGAR_XET_CAS_URL string "" URL of the Xet CAS endpoints. Default: /xet-cas. xet.token_ttlHANGAR_XET_TOKEN_TTL duration 1h Lifetime of Xet write tokens. xet.xorb_retentionHANGAR_XET_XORB_RETENTION duration 672h How long xorbs are kept after their last use, so clients can deduplicate against them. Keep it longer than hf_xet's 21-day shard cache. xet.max_file_sizeHANGAR_XET_MAX_FILE_SIZE size 50GiB Largest file a Xet upload may describe. One shard may rebuild at most four times this, counting only files not uploaded before; larger uploads get 413.

docs.title: jobs
docs.text:
Background Job workers.

Key Type Default Description jobs.workersHANGAR_JOBS_WORKERS int 4 Concurrent Jobs per worker process. jobs.leaseHANGAR_JOBS_LEASE duration 1m Lease length of a claimed Job. Renewed while the Job runs.

docs.title: gc
docs.text:
Garbage collection of unreferenced LFS objects and git data.

Key Type Default Description gc.scheduleHANGAR_GC_SCHEDULE string 0 3 * * * Cron schedule (5 fields) of the gc Job. gc.grace_periodHANGAR_GC_GRACE_PERIOD duration 168h Unreferenced LFS objects are deleted after this long.

docs.title: repos
docs.text:
Repo lifecycle.

Key Type Default Description repos.restore_windowHANGAR_REPOS_RESTORE_WINDOW duration 168h How long a deleted Repo can be restored before it is purged.

docs.title: viewer
docs.text:
Dataset Viewer and Parquet export.

Key Type Default Description viewer.enabledHANGAR_VIEWER_ENABLED bool true Turn on Parquet export and the Dataset Viewer. viewer.max_convert_bytesHANGAR_VIEWER_MAX_CONVERT_BYTES size 5GiB Splits larger than this get a partial Parquet export. viewer.max_scan_rowsHANGAR_VIEWER_MAX_SCAN_ROWS int 5000000 Rows scanned by one filter or search request before it returns partial results. viewer.max_scan_secondsHANGAR_VIEWER_MAX_SCAN_SECONDS duration 10s Time limit of one filter or search request before it returns partial results. viewer.max_cell_bytesHANGAR_VIEWER_MAX_CELL_BYTES size 100KiB Cells larger than this are truncated in Viewer responses. viewer.max_request_bytesHANGAR_VIEWER_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES size 300000000 Decoded Parquet data one Dataset Viewer request may hold; requests that need more answer with an error, as the Hub's do. viewer.convert_concurrencyHANGAR_VIEWER_CONVERT_CONCURRENCY int 1 dataset.convert Jobs per worker.

docs.title: ui
docs.text:
Web UI.

Key Type Default Description ui.docs_urlHANGAR_UI_DOCS_URL string https://hangar.page/ Where the web UI's links to the documentation go, such as a docs mirror on an air-gapped network. The mirror must serve the same paths as https://hangar.page/. Empty removes the links.

docs.title: webhooks
docs.text:
Webhook deliveries.

Key Type Default Description webhooks.allow_private_targetsHANGAR_WEBHOOKS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_TARGETS bool false Let webhooks reach private addresses: loopback, RFC 1918, carrier-grade NAT and unique local. Off by default, so users cannot make Hangar send requests into your network. Link-local and cloud metadata addresses are refused whatever this says. This is the default for the Instance setting of the same name, which an Instance admin can change under Admin, Settings.

docs.title: telemetry
docs.text:
OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and logs. Standard OTEL_* variables also apply and win.

Key Type Default Description telemetry.service_nameHANGAR_TELEMETRY_SERVICE_NAME string hangar service.name resource attribute. telemetry.environmentHANGAR_TELEMETRY_ENVIRONMENT string "" deployment.environment.name resource attribute. Empty leaves it unset. telemetry.tracesHANGAR_TELEMETRY_TRACES string otlp Trace exporter: otlp, console or none. otlp exports only when an OTLP endpoint is set with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT. Ignored when OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER is set. telemetry.metricsHANGAR_TELEMETRY_METRICS string otlp Metric exporter: otlp, prometheus, console or none. otlp exports only when an OTLP endpoint is set. Ignored when OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER is set. telemetry.logsHANGAR_TELEMETRY_LOGS string otlp Log exporter: otlp, console or none. otlp exports only when an OTLP endpoint is set. Ignored when OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER is set. Logs always go to stdout too. telemetry.prometheus_listenHANGAR_TELEMETRY_PROMETHEUS_LISTEN string :9464 Address of the Prometheus /metrics endpoint when metrics is prometheus. telemetry.log_formatHANGAR_TELEMETRY_LOG_FORMAT string json Stdout log format: json or text. telemetry.log_levelHANGAR_TELEMETRY_LOG_LEVEL string info Minimum log level: debug, info, warn or error.

docs.title: Metrics reference
docs.text:
Hangar exports these metrics over OTLP, or on /metrics when telemetry.metrics is prometheus. HTTP server and client metrics follow the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions (http.server.request.duration, http.server.active_requests and the body size histograms), and Go runtime metrics come from the runtime instrumentation. Repo IDs are never metric attributes; they are on spans and logs.

Gauges that need a database count are computed by one worker at a time every 60 seconds.
